papers.abstract: Local therapy has recently been applied to treat oligometastatic cancer across various malignant cancers. However, definitive evidence for local treatment regimens remains lacking. We aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of combining local therapy with systemic treatment for patients with oligometastatic solid tumors including breast cancer, liver cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a multicenter retrospective study. From January 2013 to December 2023, 575 patients with fewer than or equal to five metastases of breast cancer, liver cancer, and NSCLC in three tertiary university hospitals were analyzed retrospectively. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). The secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and prognostic factors affecting the treatment outcomes. Before propensity score matching, significant differences were observed in both OS and PFS between the local therapy plus systemic therapy and systemic therapy alone groups (p < 0.001 and p < 0.001). After PSM, PFS remained significantly different (p = 0.017), but OS did not (p = 0.076). In liver cancer, before PSM analysis showed a significant PFS benefit (p = 0.011), which was absent after PSM for both OS and PFS (p = 0.568 and p = 0.363). For both breast cancer and NSCLC patients, no significant differences in OS or PFS were found after PSM. Local treatment of solitary metastatic lesions showed that no statistically significant difference was observed in OS or PFS of patients with advanced oligometastatic breast, liver cancer, and NSCLC.

papers.abstract: High-temperature requirement protease A3 (HtrA3) has been implicated in the progression of various carcinomas through tissue-specific mechanisms; however, its precise role in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. We initially identified the upregulation of HtrA3 in CRC tissues through Isobaric Tags for Relative and Absolute Quantitation (iTRAQ) proteomics, which was consistent with the analysis of the CPTAC dataset. Our research further confirmed that HtrA3 is significantly upregulated in CRC tissues and associated with reduced overall survival. Functional assays showed that HtrA3 overexpression enhanced CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while HtrA3 knockdown yielded opposite effects. In HtrA3-overexpressing HCT116 cells, increased phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and FOXO1 was observed, which was reduced upon treatment with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Conversely, in HtrA3-knockdown SW480 cells, these phosphorylation levels declined but were restored with the PI3K activator 740Y-P. In vivo, HtrA3 overexpression accelerated xenograft tumor growth. These findings suggest that HtrA3 promotes CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, potentially involving PI3K-AKT-FOXO1 signaling, and support further investigation of HtrA3 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in CRC.

papers.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) is a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) with a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload and was approved by the Japan Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency in 2025 for patients with unresectable or recurrent hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer previously treated with chemotherapy. In the pivotal TROPION-Breast01 trial, most patients had received 1 or 2 prior systemic regimens. However, in routine clinical practice, Dato-DXd is often used in heavily pretreated patients, including those with prior ADC exposure. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of Dato-DXd in this population. We retrospectively analyzed 18 patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic or recurrent breast cancer who received Dato-DXd at our institution between May and December 2025. Clinical data from electronic medical records were reviewed to assess treatment efficacy and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). All patients were female, with a median age of 56 years (range, 48-81). Patients were heavily pretreated, with a median of seven prior systemic treatment lines (range, 2-11); 72.2% had previously received trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd). Median real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) was 3.2 months. Patients with prior T-DXd exposure had significantly shorter rwPFS than T-DXd-naïve patients (2.8 vs. 6.4 months, p < 0.01). TRAEs were generally mild and manageable. The most common TRAEs included alopecia, fatigue, constipation, stomatitis, nausea, and elevated liver transaminases. Five patients required dose reductions, but no treatment discontinuations or fatal events occurred. No cases of interstitial lung disease occurred. In this cohort of heavily pretreated HR+/HER2- metastatic or recurrent breast cancer, Dato-DXd showed limited clinical activity compared with clinical trials, particularly among patients previously treated with T-DXd. Nevertheless, Dato-DXd was safely administered with toxicity management. Further real-world studies are needed to optimize patient selection and treatment sequencing.

papers.abstract: Patients with clinically node-positive (cN1) breast cancer represent a heterogeneous population with evolving axillary management strategies. We evaluated whether extent of axillary nodal involvement is associated with survival in cN1 disease. A retrospective study of patients with cT1-4N1M0 breast cancer and biopsy-proven axillary metastasis (2012-2018) was performed. All patients underwent axillary ultrasound (AUS) prior to neoadjuvant systemic therapy (NST) and again before surgery. Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used for statistical analysis. Among 825 patients, most had cT2-3 (75.6%), hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2-; 73%), ductal (89.7%) carcinoma. 64.1% (529) had 1-3 abnormal nodes on pretreatment AUS, whereas 35.9% had > 3 abnormal nodes. Definitive axillary surgery consisted of axillary lymph node dissection in 83.3% and sentinel node biopsy or targeted axillary dissection in 16.7%. Pathologic complete response (pCR) rate (breast and nodes) was 22.7%; breast-only and nodal-only pCR rates were 6.4% and 11.8%, respectively. At median follow-up of 5.6 years, 5-year overall survival, breast cancer-specific survival, and event-free survival were 92%, 94%, and 91%, respectively. Overall (breast and nodes), nodal-only, and breast-only pCR were prognostic across all survival outcomes. On multivariable analysis, age, triple negative subtype, cT4 tumors, lack of pCR, and > 3 abnormal nodes on pretreatment AUS were independent predictors of worse outcomes. Among patients with cN1 breast cancer receiving NST and surgery, long-term survival outcomes were excellent. Extent of pretreatment nodal involvement by AUS was prognostic and could help to determine treatment selection in patients with cN1 disease.

papers.abstract: Most patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and peritoneal metastases (PM) face a dismal prognosis. Cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC) is a curative-intent treatment for patients with limited disease. This study assessed long-term survival and recurrence patterns. A consecutive cohort of patients with CRC-PM treated with CRS-HIPEC. Patients with complete macroscopic cytoreduction were eligible. Main outcomes were overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), peritoneal recurrence-free survival (PRFS) and recurrence patterns. In total, 440 patients were evaluated over a median follow-up of 35.2 months (IQR 25.3-68.7). Induction systemic therapy was administered to 43.1% of patients. Median DFS was 9.7 months (95% CI 8.3-11.1), and median OS was 50.2 months (95% CI 44.3-56.2). Independent prognostic factors for decreased OS were Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI) > 10, positive lymph node status (N-stage), ASA score > 2, and right-sided primary tumors. During follow-up, 71.4% of patients developed recurrent disease in the peritoneum (54.8%), lungs (22.9%), and liver (19.1%). Independent prognostic factors for decreased PRFS were lymph node metastases and higher PCI scores. Neither induction therapy nor HIPEC regimen was correlated with PRFS. Early metachronous presentation of peritoneal metastasis, also emerged as a significant adverse factor for OS, DFS and PRFS. Patients undergoing complete CRS-HIPEC achieved a favorable median OS exceeding 50 months, with approximately 30% of individuals exhibiting long-term survival indicative of cure. However, early recurrence remains a major problem and is in need for further research to improve CRS-HIPEC regimens.

papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) is the standard treatment strategy for resectable (R) and borderline resectable with venous involvement (BR-PV) pancreatic cancer (PC). However, the survival impact of completion of perioperative chemotherapy (CPC) remains unclear. We evaluated the association between CPC and overall survival (OS) and whether the Cancer and Aging Research Group (CARG) score, a tool for predicting chemotherapy-related toxicity, could predict CPC. We retrospectively reviewed a treatment-initiated cohort of patients with R or BR-PV PC who started NAC between 2019 and 2023, regardless of receipt of surgery. CPC was defined as achieving relative total dose intensity (RTDI) ≥ 80% during NAC and RTDI ≥65% during AC. Landmark Cox models starting at L2 (L2: surgery + 34 weeks) were used for OS, with multivariable adjustment for prespecified covariates. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify predictors of CPC based on clinical variables prior to NAC. Among 122 patients 52 (42.6%) achieved CPC. Among 102 patients who reached the L2 landmark, OS was significantly longer in the CPC group than in the non-CPC group (5-year, 42.8% versus 29.8%; log-rank P = 0.022). In multivariable landmark Cox analysis, non-CPC was independently associated with worse OS (HR 2.708; P = 0.008). In multivariable logistic regression, a high CARG score was independently associated with a lower likelihood of CPC (OR 0.204; P = 0.021). CPC was associated with improved OS. The CARG score may help identify patients at risk of failing to complete perioperative chemotherapy.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the surgical outcomes in a large series of patients with growing teratoma syndrome (GTS). We conducted a retrospective study of patients with GTS treated at a tertiary center between 2000 and 2025. A total of 63 patients were included in the current study. The median age at diagnosis of GTS was 25.5 years (range 7-55 years). The median interval between the initial diagnosis of ovarian immature teratoma and the occurrence of GTS was 12.3 months (range 4-367 months). Growing teratoma syndrome developed during adjuvant chemotherapy in 30/63 (47.6%), after chemotherapy in 27/63 (42.9%), and after initial surgery without chemotherapy in 6/63 (9.5%). Complete resection was achieved in 38 patients, and fertility-sparing surgery (FSS) was performed in 50 patients. Seventeen patients experienced at least one recurrence during a median follow-up period of 44 months (range 4-196 months) after initial treatment of GTS. The presence of residual disease after the initial surgery for GTS was the only factor associated with GTS recurrence (P < 0.001). Analysis of risk factors for GTS recurrence revealed no significant difference in relapse rates between FSS and radical surgery patients (30% vs 15.4%, P = 0.290). Seven of nine patients who desired pregnancy subsequently had nine spontaneous pregnancies. The overall prognosis of ovarian GTS is favorable. Optimal debulking surgery should be performed to reduce the possibility of recurrence. Fertility-sparing surgery appears feasible in carefully selected patients who wish to preserve their fertility, after comprehensive counseling on the risk of recurrence.

papers.abstract: Although open radical nephrectomy (ORN) remains the gold standard for the surgical treatment of Wilms tumor (WT), minimally invasive techniques may be used safely for selected cases. Their current development requires regular updates of surgical guidelines. We previously proposed preliminary criteria guiding robot-assisted radical nephrectomy (RARN) for WT, and, in light of our continued extensive experience, this study aimed to describe the selection of children for RARN, including a new volumetric ratio. All consecutive children who underwent ORN or RARN (2016-2023) for presumptive WT at our center were prospectively included. A volumetric ratio (preoperative tridimensional volumetry of [tumor + healthy kidney] over estimated patient's blood volume) was used to assess tumor volume. Surgical and oncological outcomes were compared between groups. Sixty radical nephrectomies were performed, including 23 RARNs (38%). No statistical difference was observed in oncological outcomes between the groups. RARN procedures in patients with a volumetric ratio <35% were performed without conversions, except for three cases with renal vein thrombus, midline crossing, and minor bleeding. Three children with a volumetric ratio <35% underwent ORN instead of RARN because of organizational issues. Approximately 40% of children in our highly selected cohort were eligible for RARN. In our experience, RARN was feasible for tumors with a volumetric ratio of <35% in the absence of renal vein thrombus, midline crossing, or adjacent-organ infiltration, with the need for external validation.

papers.abstract: Cancer-induced cachexia is a multifactorial syndrome characterized by systemic inflammation and progressive skeletal muscle and fat wasting. More than 80% pancreatic cancer patients exhibit a cachectic phenotype, which significantly contributes to the overall mortality of cancer patients. Till now, there is no FDA-approved therapy for cancer-associated cachexia that has been developed. In the present study, we have demonstrated the anti-cachectic potential of an anti-malarial compound, atovaquone. We observed that atovaquone inhibits cancer cell-conditioned media-induced myotube atrophy in a dose-dependent manner. Atovaquone treatments lead to reduced cachectic markers expression in conditioned media-treated myotubes. Further, we observed that atovaquone treatment results in reduced reactive oxygen species levels in conditioned media-treated myotubes. Mechanistically, we observed that atovaquone treatment of myotubes enhances the glycolytic capacity of conditioned-media-treated myotubes by upregulating Glut4 expression. Furthermore, we established that increased Glut4 expression is primarily driven by atovaquone-induced AMPK activation. By utilizing a syngeneic orthotopic implantation model of pancreatic cancer, we have observed that atovaquone can inhibit cachectic phenotype in tumor-bearing mice, without impacting the overall tumour growth. Overall, we have demonstrated that atovaquone exhibits anti-cachectic properties in both in vitro and in vivo model systems of pancreatic cancer-associated cachexia by modulating glycolytic capacity.

papers.abstract: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have revolutionized cancer treatment, therapeutic resistance and heterogeneous patient responses remain major clinical challenges. Current paradigms predominantly focus on amplifying effector T cells (Teffs); however, this approach frequently encounters structural bottlenecks imposed by a tumor-locked, suppressive immune homeostasis. Central to this aberrant equilibrium are regulatory T cells (Tregs), which persistently elevate immune activation thresholds and restrict durable antitumor responses. In this review, we propose a paradigm shift toward reshaping baseline T cell homeostasis, highlighting exercise as a potent, systemic physiological intervention. Regular exercise systematically counteracts tumor-induced homeostatic locking by reprogramming immune metabolism, attenuating chronic inflammation, and improving tissue perfusion. Rather than indiscriminately depleting Tregs, exercise dynamically recalibrates the Teff/Treg balance, lowering activation thresholds while preserving systemic immune tolerance. Furthermore, we propose that structured physical activity may support a form of "homeostatic memory," with potential implications for the durability of immunotherapy responses. Integrating exercise into oncological care offers a translational, host-centered strategy to optimize the immune background, thereby unlocking the full clinical potential of cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: CDK4/6 are key cell-cycle regulators. CDK4/6 inhibitors encounter obstacles from therapeutic resistance and haematological toxicity, primarily due to potent CDK6 inhibition. Developing selective inhibitors against specific CDK members could address these limitations, but faces challenges from the high homology of ATP-binding sites. SCP-7 is a sesquiterpene lactone derivative with potent anti-non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) activity. Carbamate modification yields the optimised analogue SCP-7e. Biotinylated probe-based target fishing, MCODE analysis, DARTS, CETSA, SPR, circular dichroism and tryptophan fluorescence quenching analysis identified CDK4 as the target. The binding site on CDK4 was determined by LC-MS/MS, site-directed mutagenesis and covalent molecular docking. Co-immunoprecipitation was employed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms. SCP-7 and SCP-7e selectively bind to CDK4, excluding CDK6 and promote the ubiquitin-proteasome degradation of CDK4. SCP-7e exhibits enhanced metabolic stability, superior in vivo anti-NSCLC activity, higher CDK4 binding affinity and greater degradation efficiency than SCP-7. Mechanistically, SCP-7e covalently binds to Cys78, a residue located outside the ATP-binding pocket of CDK4, thereby sterically blocking CDK4-cyclin D1 interaction and inducing SKP2-mediated degradation of CDK4. This study identified Cys78 as a novel druggable site on CDK4 and provided a selective CDK4 degrader, advancing next-generation selective CDK inhibitors.

papers.abstract: Right-sided double-lumen endobronchial tubes (DLTs) are often avoided because of technical difficulties and concerns about respiratory complications, although evidence that they increase hypoxemia during anesthesia remains limited and inconsistent. We evaluated the association between DLT side and hypoxemia during anesthesia in patients undergoing unilateral surgery for left-sided lung tumors. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients undergoing unilateral surgery for left-sided lung tumors between October 2008 and May 2023. The primary outcome was hypoxemia during anesthesia, defined as SpO2 ≤ 90% for at least 3 consecutive min during the anesthetic period. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to adjust for measured differences between patients receiving right-sided and left-sided DLTs. Odds ratios (ORs) and absolute risk differences (RDs) were estimated. Among 1,280 patients, 842 received right-sided DLTs and 438 received left-sided DLTs. After overlap weighting, measured covariates were well balanced. The incidence of hypoxemia during anesthesia was 20.0% with right-sided DLTs and 18.5% with left-sided DLTs (OR, 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68-1.79; P = 0.70). The RD was 1.51 percentage points (95% CI - 3.86-6.87). No clear between-group differences were observed in exploratory secondary respiratory outcomes. We found no clear evidence that right-sided DLT use was associated with a higher incidence of hypoxemia during anesthesia than left-sided DLT use. However, equivalence between the two devices was not established, and further studies are needed to determine whether clinically important differences in hypoxemia risk exist.

papers.abstract: Chemotherapy combined with programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) antibody immunotherapy has become the standard first-line treatment for most patients with malignant solid tumors. However, data from multiple phase III trials indicate that even with first-line induction followed by immunotherapy maintenance, median progression-free survival (PFS) remains less than one year. In this phase I dose-escalation trial (3 + 3 design), 12 patients who completed six cycles of first-line chemoimmunotherapy received oral fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) capsules plus anti-PD-1 maintenance immunotherapy at escalating dose levels (i to i + 3). The primary endpoint was safety; secondary endpoints included the recommended phase II dose (RP2D), PFS, and disease control rate (DCR). Fecal and blood samples were collected for exploratory microbiome and metabolomic analyses. No grade ≥3 FMT-related toxicities occurred. With a median follow-up of 36.9 months, median PFS was 19.8 months (95% CI 11.2-28.4); maintenance-phase PFS was 11.7 months (95% CI 4.1-19.3). 4 patients remained progression-free on continued immunotherapy. Four patients (33.3%) experienced grade 1-2 gastrointestinal events. Microbiomic analyses showed post-FMT expansion of Blautia and Faecalibacterium, with dose level i + 1 demonstrating the greatest α-diversity shift and engraftment rate. Metabolomic analysis showed that serum arachidonic acid levels increased after FMT. Oral FMT combined with immunotherapy as first-line maintenance therapy for solid tumors was safe and well tolerated, showed promising preliminary efficacy, and induced favorable compositional changes in the gut microbiota. This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No.: ChiCTR2100054928).

papers.abstract: In robotic pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD) for tumors with portal vein (PV) involvement and a replaced right hepatic artery (rRHA), precise dissection from the posterior aspect of the pancreatic head is not always straightforward. Therefore, an anterior and inferior approach may be more appropriate in the robotic setting. The rRHA should be identified at both its proximal and distal ends (at its origin from the superior mesenteric artery [SMA] and along the right side of the bile duct within the hepatoduodenal ligament, respectively) and dissected from both sides to the greatest extent feasible.1 The key principle is to obtain proximal and distal control of the rRHA before approaching the most adherent portion of the tumor. Unlike standard RPD, the presence of an rRHA requires early identification and vascular control from both its proximal and distal sides before PV/superior mesenteric vein (SMV) dissection because the artery may limit posterior exposure and is at risk during dissection of the tumor from the portomesenteric vein.

papers.abstract: The nerve-sparing (NS) technique may reduce urinary and erectile dysfunction in patients with localized prostate cancer undergoing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). However, the influence of NS dissection depth on functional outcomes remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the impact of NS grades, based on a four-layer dissection model, on urinary continence and nerve function using subjective and objective outcome measures. This was a retrospective cohort of 600 consecutive patients undergoing RARP (December 2012-September 2023), with NS graded I-IV (intrafascial to extrafascial) using surgical records/videos. Maximum NS grade (mNSG) was defined as the highest grade on either side. Continence was defined as using no safety pad or only one safety pad/day. Urodynamic study and intraoperative electrical stimulation were used in a subset to evaluate urinary and nerve function. Associations between NS grade and outcomes were assessed using logistic regression. Patients with mNSG I showed significantly better continence at 3, 6, and 12 months (p < 0.001, p < 0.001, p = 0.017, respectively). A total number of both sides of ≥ 3 (NS grade I to IV = point 3 to 0) was also associated with better continence. mNSG I remained an independent predictor at 3 and 6 months. Urodynamic study parameters were largely comparable, except for higher voiding volume in mNSG I (p = 0.006). Greater preservation of intraurethral pressure after stimulation was observed in mNSG I. Limitations include the retrospective design and selection bias. Even unilateral intrafascial NS (mNSG I) may improve continence and nerve function. papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, immune-mediated disorder of the gastrointestinal tract and an escalating global public health challenge, particularly in newly industrializing regions. Its etiology and pathogenesis remain incompletely understood, although disrupted homeostasis between the intestinal microbiota and the mucosal immune system is implicated. Macrophages and T cells contribute to the balance between tissue injury and repair. Increasing evidence suggests that metabolic state and epigenetic programs interact to influence immune cell function. Under hypoxic and inflammatory stress, glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism can undergo remodeling, including shifts between glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation, altered fatty-acid utilization, changes in tryptophan and methionine metabolism, and fluctuations in methyl-donor availability. Metabolic cues may influence chromatin regulation and immune signaling through acetylation, methylation, lactylation, palmitoylation, phosphorylation, and other modifications. These processes can affect effector programs, the T helper 17-regulatory T cell balance, macrophage inflammatory gene expression, inflammasome activation, and interleukin-10-related signaling, with potential implications for mucosal barrier repair and inflammatory amplification. However, the causal roles of these metabolic and epigenetic alterations in IBD remain to be clarified: they may contribute to disease initiation, arise as accompanying features of the disease state, or amplify inflammation once it is established. This review synthesizes current advances in metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic regulation in macrophages and T cells, examining immunometabolic nodes that link environmental stress to chromatin remodeling. We further summarize emerging therapeutic strategies targeting metabolic and epigenetic pathways, assess evidence from preclinical and clinical studies, and discuss interventions directed at immunometabolic checkpoints.

papers.abstract: Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([18F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [18F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [18F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

papers.abstract: Platinum resistance remains the principal obstacle to improving survival in ovarian cancer. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is associated with chemoresistance and immune remodeling, but the molecular regulators connecting vascular invasion, innate immune-driven inflammatory amplification, and treatment failure remain poorly defined. Three public datasets and 118 literature-curated MVI genes were integrated. Differential expression analysis followed by three-way intersection identified PAQR5 as the core candidate. Its clinical, immune-inflammatory, and pharmacological relevance was mapped using CIBERSORT, ESTIMATE, pRRophetic, and nomogram modeling, and validated by qPCR/Western blot, MTT/CCK-8, colony/wound-healing assays, flow cytometry, gamma-H2AX foci, EdU incorporation, and subcutaneous xenografts (n = 5-6 mice/group). PAQR5 was the only gene shared among cisplatin-resistance signatures in vitro (303 DEGs), patient tissue resistance signatures (2507 DEGs), and the MVI gene set. TCGA tumors overexpressed PAQR5 2.8-fold compared with GTEx normal tissue (P < 0.001). High PAQR5 independently predicted shortened overall survival (HR = 1.18; 95% CI 1.02-1.44; P = 0.005) and 5-year progression-free survival (HR = 1.33; 95% CI 1.09-1.63; P = 0.04). In silico, PAQR5-high tumors showed an innate immune-skewed suppressive profile, with increased M2 macrophages (+28%) and Tregs (+17%) but reduced CD8+ T cells (-31%) and NK cells (-21%; all P < 0.01). They also displayed elevated cisplatin, docetaxel, and paclitaxel IC50 values (each P < 0.0001), whereas AKT-inhibitor VIII IC50 fell 1.7-fold. Functionally, PAQR5 overexpression increased proliferation, colony formation, migration, DNA damage tolerance, and xenograft growth, whereas silencing produced mirror-image suppression and restored cisplatin-induced apoptosis. PAQR5 appears to couple MVI with platinum resistance by coordinating an immunosuppressive inflammatory tumor microenvironment, enhanced DNA damage repair, and reduced apoptosis. These findings nominate PAQR5 as a mechanism-linked biomarker and a therapeutic entry point for targeting inflammation-associated chemoresistance in ovarian cancer.

papers.abstract: A substantial proportion of childhood cancers occur in children who are genetically predisposed to develop that cancer. Close surveillance of children with cancer predisposition syndromes enables early cancer detection and results in better survival outcomes and less therapy-related toxicity, although many more predisposition syndromes are likely to exist and remain undetected. Building on conventional clinical surveillance protocols, new approaches are being explored, including liquid biopsy, molecular or metabolic biomarkers, enhanced imaging and microbiome profiling for the purposes of both improved surveillance and the discovery of additional predisposing factors. Knowing the specific genes, expressed proteins and biological pathways associated with a specific cancer predisposition syndrome might permit the use of targeted agents or vaccines, as well as the introduction of lifestyle changes to delay, reduce or even eliminate the development of cancer. Preclinical studies investigating the risks and benefits of preventive interventions would be greatly aided by the identification or development of animal models that faithfully recapitulate human syndromes. The incorporation of artificial intelligence to complement the clinical and experimental assessment of cancer risk based on the syndrome, genotype, modifier genes, family history, environmental exposures and other factors will undoubtedly improve the management and, ultimately, the outcomes of children with an increased genetic risk of cancer. In this Perspective, we discuss strategies to identify new cancer predisposition genes, developing approaches to cancer surveillance, emerging efforts for cancer prevention in high-risk patients, and the role of artificial intelligence in improving data analysis and optimizing medical decision-making.

papers.abstract: Gait is increasingly recognized as a vital sign, yet current approaches treat it as a symptom of specific pathologies rather than a systemic biomarker. Here we developed a gait foundation model for three-dimensional skeletal motion, which was recorded via a single-depth camera during 5 motor tasks, from 3,328 deeply phenotyped adults. Our purpose was to capture the full pattern of a person's movement and use it to predict health phenotypes such as grip strength and sleep quality across 18 body systems. Gait is conventionally described by engineered features (for example, calculated measurements such as cadence and stride length), which may fail to capture the fine detail of how a person moves. Our model instead translates movement into learned embeddings: sets of numbers that describe how all body joints move together over time. Learned embeddings outperformed engineered features for prediction of age (Pearson's r = 0.69), body mass index (r = 0.91) and visceral adipose tissue area (r = 0.83), and embeddings significantly predicted 1,887 of 3,210 tested phenotypes. Relative to a baseline model using age, body mass index, visceral adipose tissue and height alone, gait embeddings improved prediction in all 18 systems in males and 17 of 18 in females, as well as prediction of clinical diagnoses and medication use. Anatomical ablation analyses revealed that leg dynamics dominated metabolic and frailty predictions, and torso dynamics encoded sleep and lifestyle phenotypes. These findings establish gait as an independent, multisystem biosignal, motivating integration of gait analysis into routine clinical assessment as a scalable, passive vital sign.

papers.abstract: To elucidate the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response (DDR) network, we conduct unbiased genetic interaction screens using Cas12a. We disrupt 233 DDR genes frequently mutated in cancer and other genetic diseases, either individually or in pairwise combinations, enabling us to assess the phenotypic effects induced by the loss of DDR gene pairs under unperturbed cell growth conditions. We identify high-confidence positive and negative gene-gene interactions, along with connections between previously unlinked DDR pathways. Among the identified genetic interactions, we uncover synthetic lethal interactions between genes encoding the translesion polymerase REV1-Pol ζ complex and the MCM8-MCM9-HROB DNA helicase complex, between Fanconi anemia genes and various mitotic DNA repair genes, as well as between genes encoding the DNA translocase SMARCAL1 and components of the FANCM complex, suggesting opportunities for targeted treatments in tumors carrying mutations in these genes. Collectively, our genetic map of the DDR network identifies synthetic lethal and buffering interactions with therapeutic potential.

papers.abstract: Women undergoing pelvic radiotherapy are at risk of developing sarcopenia, defined by muscle loss. In patients treated with radiotherapy for cervical cancer, post-treatment muscle loss has been associated with poorer cancer-specific and overall survival. This study aimed to longitudinally assess sarcopenia and changes in muscle during radiotherapy and follow-up, and to evaluate whether bioelectrical impedance analysis can serve as an accurate bedside alternative to computed tomography (CT) for sarcopenia assessment. This prospective cohort study included women with histologically confirmed primary cervical, endometrial, vulvar, or vaginal cancer, all scheduled to undergo external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with curative intent. Sarcopenia was assessed at baseline, during the last week of EBRT, and at the three- and six-month follow-up. Two methods were used to evaluate sarcopenia: lumbar skeletal muscle index measured via CT scan (gold standard) and appendicular skeletal muscle mass via bioelectrical impedance analysis. Fisher's exact test and the Mann-Whitney U test were used to compare baseline characteristics between women with and without sarcopenia during the last week of radiotherapy. A total of 31 women were included. Based on CT scans, the prevalence of sarcopenia was 23% at baseline, 32% at the last week of radiotherapy, and 42% at the three-month follow-up. At the six-month follow-up, 29% of the women were sarcopenic. Bioelectrical impedance analysis detected sarcopenia in only 0% to 50% of cases across the various time points. Patients with FIGO stage III were significantly more frequently sarcopenic based on their appendicular skeletal muscle index as assessed by CT scan during the last week of EBRT. The prevalence of sarcopenia is high in women treated with radiotherapy for gynecological cancer. An increase in the prevalence of sarcopenia was observed, reaching its highest point at the three-month follow-up. Sarcopenia may be underestimated when assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, as indicated by the low sensitivity observed.

papers.abstract: To describe lower anterior access single-port robotic radical nephroureterectomy (LAA-SP RNU), including bladder cuff excision (BCE) and lymph node dissection (LND), without repositioning or redocking. We present a multicenter retrospective series of 47 patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma who underwent LAA-SP RNU at five referral centers (May 2024-July 2025). A single 4-cm extraperitoneal incision enabled nephroureterectomy, BCE, and selective hilar/pelvic LND without repositioning or redocking. Data were evaluated using descriptive analyses, and pentafecta achievement for the full cohort was estimated through Kaplan-Meier analysis. Median age of the patients was 72 yr; 95% had high-risk disease. LND was performed in 20 patients (43%). Median docking and operative times were 20 and 220 min, respectively; one procedure was converted to open surgery. Grade ≥3 complications occurred in three patients (6%); median hospital stay was 5 d. Pathology showed pT2 and pT3 disease in 15% and 36%, respectively. At median follow-up of 12.3 mo, seven patients (14.9%) experienced recurrence, including five intravesical recurrences; two died from metastatic disease. The 12-mo Kaplan-Meier estimate of pentafecta achievement was 76.7% (95% confidence interval, 62.8-90.5%). This study is limited by potential referral-center and patient-selection bias, heterogeneity in LND and postoperative management, limited follow-up, and the absence of cost-effectiveness data. LAA-SP RNU appears feasible and associated with acceptable perioperative and early oncological outcomes in experienced centers. Comparative prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to establish oncological durability, patient benefit, and cost-effectiveness.

papers.abstract: SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma (RMC) is a rare, highly aggressive malignancy affecting predominantly young individuals with sickle hemoglobinopathies. However, no disease-specific prognostic tools exist. We aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic model for overall survival using routinely available variables measured at diagnosis. This single-institution retrospective cohort study included 180 patients with SMARCB1-deficient RMC (2003-2025). In total, 16 prespecified candidate predictors were evaluated. For internal validation, the complete variable and distribution selection process was repeated within 1000 bootstrap resamples across 50 multiply imputed datasets. Coefficients of the final log-normal accelerated failure time model were uniformly shrunk by the resulting optimism-corrected calibration slope, and clinical utility was assessed by 24-mo decision curve analysis (DCA). Renal Medullary Carcinoma Clinical and Outcomes Model for Prognostic Assessment and Survival Stratification (RMC-COMPASS) retained Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, number of involved anatomic disease sites beyond the primary tumor, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and corrected calcium. The optimism-corrected C-index was 0.64 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.61-0.71) and the calibration slope was 0.895 (95% CI 0.589-1.20). RMC-COMPASS showed higher discrimination than the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium score (C-index 0.58) and DCA demonstrated positive net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds. Limitations include the single-institution design and lack of external validation. RMC-COMPASS is the first internally validated prognostic model for SMARCB1-deficient RMC. It provides individualized survival estimates through a freely available web-based calculator (https://trialdesign.org/one-page-shell.html#RMC-COMPASS) to support prognostic counseling, while prespecified risk groups are intended for stratification in future prospective studies. The model is not validated for treatment selection and requires external validation before routine clinical use.

papers.abstract: To compare para-aortic recurrence, survival outcomes, and treatment-related toxicity between prophylactic extended-field irradiation (EFI) and pelvic radiotherapy (PRT) in patients with high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) who have radiologically negative para-aortic lymph nodes (PALNs). We retrospectively reviewed patients with FIGO 2018 stage III-IVA cervical cancer treated with definitive radiotherapy or concurrent chemoradiotherapy between December 2015 and December 2022. Eligible patients had radiologically negative PALNs and at least one high-risk feature: ≥2 positive pelvic lymph nodes, a maximum pelvic nodal short-axis diameter ≥ 1.5 cm, or pelvic sidewall involvement. Patients received EFI (n = 140) or PRT (n = 153). Survival outcomes were compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. Para-aortic recurrence occurred in 2.1% of patients receiving EFI and 11.1% receiving PRT. Five-year PARFS, PFS, and DMFS were higher with EFI than with PRT (97.8% vs 88.1%, P = 0.002; 70.9% vs 58.8%, P = 0.002; and 83.7% vs 75.2%, P = 0.032, respectively). Five-year OS was 79.1% versus 68.6% (P = 0.052). In multivariable analysis, EFI remained associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.532; P = 0.002), DMFS (HR, 0.554; P = 0.036), and PARFS (HR, 0.178; P = 0.006), but not OS (HR, 0.630; P = 0.054). Grade 3-4 leukopenia was more frequent with EFI, whereas other severe toxicities were similar. Prophylactic EFI was associated with improved para-aortic control, PFS, and DMFS in high-risk LACC, with acceptable toxicity. These findings support further evaluation of a risk-adapted strategy for selecting patients who may benefit from prophylactic EFI.

papers.abstract: Metabolic plasticity enables tumors to adapt to fluctuating nutrient environments, yet the non-canonical functions of metabolic enzymes under stress remain largely unexplored. Here, we established a pyrimidine biosynthesis-associated gene score (PBAGS) that predicts survival in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and identified dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) as a critical driver with a context-dependent dual role. Under glucose-replete conditions, DHODH functions as a canonical oncogene, promoting pyrimidine and cysteine metabolism, alongside UDP-GlcNAc production; accordingly, its inhibition by leflunomide suppresses tumor growth. Strikingly, under glucose starvation, DHODH undergoes a functional switch to become a "molecular executioner." Mechanistically, starvation triggers the DHODH-OGT axis to maintain site-specific O-GlcNAcylation of SLC7A11 at Ser26, thereby stabilizing SLC7A11. This modification promotes excessive cystine accumulation and subsequent actin cytoskeleton collapse, ultimately triggering disulfidptosis. Accordingly, inhibition of DHODH abolishes this modification and rescues cells from starvation-induced death. Clinically, DHODH-SLC7A11 axis correlates tightly with GLUT1 expression. Mimicking glucose starvation using GLUT1 inhibitor BAY-876 significantly enhances radiosensitivity in ESCC PDX models that harbor high DHODH/SLC7A11 expression. Collectively, our findings uncover that under glucose starvation, DHODH and SLC7A11 co-dependency synergistically promotes disulfidptosis, suggesting that targeting the metabolic context offers a potent strategy to sensitize ESCC to radiotherapy.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to escalate the dose to the residual primary tumor with an adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) boost after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and to explore, within this cohort, whether a higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control (LRC) and whether this translated into a difference in overall survival (OS). In this single-center, prospective, single-arm cohort, 51 patients received concurrent CRT (50 Gy/25 fractions with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel) followed by an adaptive boost (30 Gy/5 fractions to the residual primary, 10 Gy/5 fractions to residual nodes), without consolidation durvalumab. Doses were summed by deformable registration and reported as EQD2. Response was assessed at 3 months with FDG-PET/CT (PERCIST), and toxicity with CTCAE v5.0. Outcomes estimated by Kaplan-Meier; predictors by Cox regression. At a median follow-up of 26 months, 2-year OS and LRC were 61.5% and 62.8%. The median PFS and DMFS were 13 and 16 months, and distant metastasis was the dominant failure pattern (41.2%). Cumulative dose below 94.77 Gy (EQD2) to the residual primary independently predicted worse LRC (HR 5.86), and a 3-month locoregional SUVmax ≥4.55 predicted worse LRC (HR 5.04). OS was independently associated with residual nodal volume, 3-month metabolic progression, and subsequent locoregional progression. Grade 3-4 pneumonitis occurred in 7.8%, grade 3 esophagitis in one patient (2%), and hemoptysis in five (9.8%). The SBRT boost achieved encouraging locoregional control, including in bulky and node-advanced disease, without immunotherapy, and higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control. Hemoptysis was the main safety concern and occurred predominantly in patients with pre-existing hemoptysis, supporting careful selection and strict bronchial constraints. Local escalation alone did not overcome the competing risk of distant failure.

papers.abstract: Biglycan (BGN) is an important component of the extracellular matrix (ECM). Using an integrated analysis of TCGA bulk RNA-sequencing, single-cell RNA-sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic datasets, we systematically characterized the expression patterns, prognostic significance, and biological roles of BGN in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and survival analyses in independent clinical cohorts further validated the expression pattern, abundance, and prognostic significance of BGN. The biological role of BGN was further investigated using in vitro tumor cell-cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) co-culture systems, BGN knockdown, and subsequent phenotypic assays. Here, BGN was significantly upregulated in HNSCC tissues, and elevated BGN expression was associated with poorer patient prognosis. Higher BGN expression was also associated with increased mesenchymal scores, enrichment of pathways related to CAF activation, ECM remodeling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), as well as potentially reduced sensitivity to commonly used chemotherapeutic agents. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that BGN was predominantly expressed by CAFs, with BGN-positive (BGN+) CAFs exhibiting markedly enhanced ECM remodeling activity and greater potential for intercellular communication. Spatial transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that BGN-high spots were preferentially localized within the stromal matrix and distant from the tumor core. Functionally, tumor cells co-cultured with BGN-knockdown CAFs exhibited reduced proliferation, colony-forming capacity, invasion, and migration, accompanied by suppression of the EMT phenotype. Collectively, these findings suggest that BGN may serve as a biomarker of an ECM/stromal remodeling-dominant CAF state in HNSCC and represent a potential therapeutic target for HNSCC.

papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by high aggressiveness and limited therapeutic options. However, the molecular determinants driving ccRCC progression and therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined. Through integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses, we identified HAUS5 as a tumor-enriched factor that was highly expressed in ccRCC tissues and tumor-derived epithelial cells. Elevated HAUS5 expression was associated with adverse clinicopathological features and poor overall survival. Functional assays showed that HAUS5 depletion suppressed ccRCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft tumor growth. Mechanistically, HAUS5 was associated with MAPK/ERK signaling activation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, whereas EGF partially rescued the inhibitory effects induced by HAUS5 knockdown. In addition, drug sensitivity analysis identified Belinostat as a candidate compound associated with HAUS5 expression, and functional experiments showed that Belinostat attenuated HAUS5-associated malignant phenotypes. Collectively, these findings suggest that HAUS5 contributes to ccRCC progression through a MAPK/ERK-associated EMT program and may be linked to differential sensitivity to Belinostat.

papers.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is characterized by a dense desmoplastic microenvironment dominated by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which profoundly shape tumor behavior and diminish therapeutic efficacy. By integrating analyses of patient specimens with multi-omics profiling, mechanistic assays, tumor-CAF co-culture and xenograft models, and single-cell transcriptomics, we identified retinoic acid receptor γ (RARγ) as a central regulator of reciprocal communication between malignant cells and CAFs that promotes ferroptosis resistance. RARγ was markedly elevated in CAF-enriched tumors and associated with poor overall survival. Multi-omics integration revealed that RARγ increases CREB stability and reduces K33- and K48-linked polyubiquitination, thereby enhancing CREB occupancy at the AKR1C1 promoter and driving transcriptional activation. AKR1C1 subsequently reinforces the Nrf2-GPX4 antioxidant axis, elevates glutathione metabolism, and suppresses lipid peroxidation. Beyond intrinsic protection, RARγ induces LCN2 transcription and promotes exosomal packaging of LCN2, which is transferred to adjacent CAFs and triggers robust CSF3 (G-CSF) secretion. CAF-derived G-CSF feeds back to malignant cells to amplify RARγ expression and ferroptotic tolerance, forming a self-sustaining paracrine circuit. Single-cell RNA sequencing further supported coordinated interactions between RARG+ tumor subsets and CSF3+ CAFs, reinforcing the relevance of this signaling loop in human CCA. Collectively, these findings position RARγ as a master organizer of tumor-stroma crosstalk through the CREB-AKR1C1 and LCN2-CSF3 axes, establishing a ferroptosis-resistant niche and promoting CCA aggressiveness.

papers.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) testing can identify molecular residual disease after radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), yet it remains unknown how clinicians have adopted it into practice. We evaluated trends in ctDNA testing and its association with adjuvant therapy. Using the Flatiron Health Research Database, we identified adults with nonmetastatic MIBC diagnosed on or after 1 January 2021, who underwent radical cystectomy and had at least 12 weeks of observable follow-up. The primary exposure was a documented postcystectomy ctDNA result (Signatera), defined by a result report 4-24 weeks after cystectomy. Logistic regression evaluated trends in documented results. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted risk ratios (RRs) for adjuvant therapy within 24 weeks among patients whose ctDNA result preceded the treatment decision. Among 4533 patients, the median age was 70 years, 77.4% were male, and 74.6% were White. The odds of a documented ctDNA result increased by 16% per calendar quarter [odds ratio (OR) 1.16, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.13-1.19]. Patients with high-risk pathology were nearly twice as likely to have a documented result (9.0% versus 5.3%; RR 1.71, 95% CI 1.35-2.17). Patients with a documented result more often received adjuvant therapy than patients without (49.6% versus 33.5%; RR 1.48, 95% CI 1.32-1.66). Among 200 patients whose ctDNA result preceded the treatment decision, detectable ctDNA (n = 59) was associated with greater adjuvant therapy use in unadjusted analysis (45.8% versus 21.3%; RR 2.15, 95% CI 1.41-3.28), but this association was attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment (adjusted RR 1.34, 95% CI 0.89-2.02). High-risk pathology remained strongly associated with treatment (adjusted RR 9.45, 95% CI 3.07-29.10). Postcystectomy ctDNA testing increased rapidly, particularly among patients with high-risk pathology. Pathologic risk remained the factor most strongly associated with adjuvant treatment, whereas the association with detectable ctDNA was attenuated after adjustment, although precision was limited.

papers.abstract: Poorly differentiated thyroid cancer (PDTC) lacks a dedicated staging system, requiring use of the eighth version of the American Joint Committee on Cancer and Union for International Cancer Control TNM staging system (TNM-8) for differentiated thyroid cancer despite its distinct biology. To develop a PDTC-specific staging system. This cohort study analyzed data from the International Aggressive Thyroid Cancer Collaborative Group (IATCCG), including surgically treated patients at 91 centers in 14 countries from January 1984 to January 2026. External validation was performed using patients from the US Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Data were analyzed from December 2025 to June 2026. The primary end point was overall survival. With M1 disease predefined as stage IVB, the schema for stages I-IVA in patients with M0 disease were redefined. All possible TN combinations were fitted into multivariable Cox models, with the lowest Akaike information criterion defining the proposed system. Prognostic discrimination was assessed using adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and C statistics. Among 1010 patients in the IATCCG cohort, 610 (60.4%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at diagnosis was 58 (46-68) years; median (IQR) follow-up was 41 (15-85) months. Among 170 patients in the SEER cohort, 85 (50.0%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at diagnosis was 61 (49-72) years; median (IQR) follow-up was 92 (42-154) months. In the IATCCG cohort, level VII lymph node metastasis (LNM) was associated with lower 5-year overall survival (45.2%; 95% CI, 33.4-61.2) than level VI (73.2%; 95% CI, 64.4-83.3) or lateral neck LNM (56.7%; 95% CI, 49.4-65.0). Level VII LNM was therefore reclassified from N1a to N1c. The lowest Akaike information criterion configuration among 16 738 candidates defined stages I to IVA as follows: I, T1N0/NX/N1a or T2N0/NX; II, T1N1b/N1c, T2N1a/N1b, or T3N0/NX/N1a; III, T2N1c, T3N1b, or T4aN0/NX/N1a; IVA, T3N1c, T4aN1b/N1c, or T4b any N; and IVB, M1 disease. Compared with TNM-8, stage I disease decreased from 44.4% (448 of 1010) to 24.6% (248 of 1010) and stage IV disease increased from 18.5% (187 of 1010) to 32.4% (327 of 1010) with the proposed system. The proposed staging had a higher C statistic than TNM-8 (0.74 [95% CI, 0.71-0.76] vs 0.71 [95% CI, 0.68-0.74]; difference, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.01-0.04). Corresponding SEER C statistic values were 0.76 (95% CI, 0.71-0.81) vs 0.74 (95% CI, 0.68-0.79), respectively (difference, 0.02; 95% CI, -0.01 to 0.06). This cohort study found that this PDTC-specific staging system provides improved prognostic stratification reflecting its different biology. These data provide a strong rationale for the potential inclusion of a stand-alone American Joint Committee on Cancer staging system for PDTC.

papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) treatment remains hindered by three intertwined challenges, drug delivery barriers, immune evasion, and high relapse rates. Despite advances in nanocarriers and immunomodulation, an integrated platform that achieves precise targeting, potent sterilisation, immune remodelling, and durable protection is still lacking. A biomimetic DNA tetrahedral phototherapy system (TDN + AIE@MM) was constructed using Mycobacterium marinum membrane modification to mimic trained immunity and enable dual spatiotemporal targeting of granulomas and lymph nodes. Through natural membrane ligand recognition, the system delivered payloads to immunosuppressive granulomas and antigen-retarded lymph nodes. Upon NIR-II irradiation, the AIE agent generated local hyperthermia to kill intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis and released antigens to activate adaptive and long-term memory immune responses. TDN + AIE@MM exhibited uniform size, good stability, and preserved membrane proteins. In vitro, it showed superior targeting to H37Ra and macrophages over unmodified controls. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, it achieved >99% killing of extra- and intracellular H37Ra, induced M1 polarisation with pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α), and enhanced T-cell proliferation and antigen-specific responses. In vivo, it achieved spatiotemporal dual-targeting to granulomas and lymph nodes, increased CD80+/CD86+ antigen-presenting cells and CD4+ T-cell activation, and reduced lung bacterial load. For immune memory, TRM (CD8+CD69+CD103+) reached 21.8% on day 42, approximately two-fold higher than rifampicin (Rif). In a rechallenge relapse model, the 84-day relapse rate was 16.7% versus 66.7% for Rif, with higher memory B cells and TEM, confirming durable protection. These findings show that TDN + AIE@MM integrates physical sterilisation, immunosuppression reversal, and durable immune memory via dual spatiotemporal targeting, effectively addressing the three core challenges in TB therapy, namely delivery barriers, immune evasion, and relapse risk, and offering a promising strategy for immunotherapy and relapse prevention. papers.abstract: We characterize the spatiotemporal dynamics of the tumor microenvironment (TME) in bladder cancer (BLCA) samples before and after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in a multicenter real-world cohort (n = 606). We identify two distinct differentiation outcomes in BLCA epithelial cells: sensitivity and resistance to immunotherapy. Additionally, we identify SERPINH1 as a common target of acquired immunotherapy resistance in BLCA. Furthermore, we characterize an immunotherapy-induced tumor-myeloid barrier, which leads to an excluded immune phenotype and immunotherapy resistance. Finally, we identify T cell terminal exhaustion and a senescent inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblast phenotype as key factors contributing to immunotherapy resistance. Collectively, we reveal the dynamic phenotypic evolution of the TME in BLCA during neoadjuvant immunotherapy and identify the characteristics of residual lesions after immunotherapy. These findings enrich our understanding of immunotherapy resistance in BLCA and contribute to developing combination therapies to improve patient prognosis.

papers.abstract: Postoperative pain management remains a critical issue in peri-operative medicine, but contemporary national data are lacking. AlgoSFAR 2 was a prospective, multicentre and observational study, conducted in randomly selected French surgical centres. Adult patients undergoing elective surgery were included. Pain was assessed at rest and during mobilization over the first three postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included postoperative opioid consumption and multimodal analgesia strategies defined as the use of at least two non-opioid strategies such as analgesics and/or regional anaesthesia. A total of 3879 patients from 80 centres were analysed. While pre-operative and immediate postoperative pain levels at rest were low, pain peaked on day 1, with high interindividual variability, and 6% of patients reported severe pain. Two thirds (66%) did not need any rescue opioids postoperatively. Overall, 95% received multimodal analgesia. These results highlight a major change in postoperative pain management in France, with broad adoption of multimodal opioid-sparing strategies. Nonetheless, a minority of patients still experience severe pain, highlighting the need for personalized management. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06487442.

papers.abstract: Sex may influence patients' response to chemotherapy or immunotherapy given before or after radical cystectomy. We reviewed all otherwise eligible prospective perioperative interventional studies, including randomized controlled trials and single-arm studies, to determine how often female enrollment, efficacy outcomes, and safety outcomes were reported separately for women and men. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched for phase 1-3 prospective interventional studies, including randomized controlled trials and single-arm studies, evaluating perioperative systemic therapy for nonmetastatic muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) between 1990 and 2024. Eligibility was based on disease setting, perioperative intervention, prospective design, and full-text availability; reporting of sex-specific outcomes was not required for inclusion and was instead coded as a review outcome. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted female enrollment and published sex-stratified efficacy or safety outcomes, and assessed risk of bias using design-appropriate tools. Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 was applied to randomized trials and the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS) to noncomparative single-arm studies. Outcomes of interest were the proportion of studies reporting efficacy or adverse events (AEs) by sex, the proportion reporting formal sex-by-treatment interaction tests, and the sex-specific hazard ratios (HRs), response rates, or survival estimates provided. Twenty-nine reports of 27 unique prospective perioperative trials were included, comprising 21 neoadjuvant and eight adjuvant reports, covering 6376 patients; 1140 (18%) were women. Female enrollment was 17% in neoadjuvant chemotherapy trials, 17% in neoadjuvant immunotherapy trials, 17% in adjuvant chemotherapy trials, and 22% in adjuvant immunotherapy trials. Five reports (17%) reported any sex-disaggregated efficacy outcome, whereas none reported AEs by sex. The pooled Nordic neoadjuvant series reported a female-versus-male HR >1 for overall survival (HR 1.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.97-1.92), although the estimate was imprecise. PURE-01 reported an imprecise female-versus-male event-free survival estimate (HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.44-3.00). In the adjuvant setting, individual cisplatin-based trials provided limited and mostly descriptive sex-specific information, whereas CheckMate-274 nivolumab reported disease-free survival estimates for women (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.38-1.06) and men (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.52-0.83), with the reported interaction test not providing clear evidence of heterogeneity (p = 0.58). Among randomized trials, risk of bias was low in eight reports, raised some concerns in eight, and was high in one; single-arm studies scored 12-15 of 16 on MINORS. Reliance on published summaries, limited female representation, and heterogeneous study designs limited formal inference. Women remain underrepresented in perioperative MIBC trials and are absent from safety reporting. The available evidence is insufficient to determine whether clinically meaningful sex-based differences in benefit exist, and modest sex-based differences cannot be excluded. Future trials should ensure balanced recruitment, stratify randomization by sex when randomization is used, and report disaggregated efficacy and toxicity outcomes to support equitable care.

papers.abstract: In severe postpartum haemorrhage (PPH), hypofibrinogenaemia is strongly associated with bleeding severity. To correct fibrinogen depletion, various fixed dosing regimens have been evaluated, but the optimal fibrinogen dosing regimen remains unknown. To date, fibrinogen pharmacokinetics have only been studied outside haemorrhagic settings (healthy or afibrinogenaemic patients) METHODS: This ancillary analysis of the TRACES trial assessed fibrinogen kinetics in 142 women with PPH > 800 ml during caesarean section, among which 31 received fibrinogen replacement. Plasma fibrinogen concentrations (n = 593) were measured using the Clauss method. A population pharmacokinetic model was developed using nonlinear mixed-effects modeling. Simulations were performed to estimate loading and maintenance doses required to achieve target fibrinogen concentrations. A one-compartment logistic model adequately described plasma fibrinogen levels. Bleeding rate was identified as a key covariate to explain fibrinogen loss rate. Based on the estimated model, an optimised dosing regimen was derived to achieve and maintain predefined target fibrinogen levels. To achieve a target increase of 1 g.L-¹ in plasma fibrinogen level, the required fibrinogen loading dose is at least 2.7 g for a body weight of 50 kg. To maintain plasma fibrinogen level at a target of 2 g.L-¹ during a 1000 mL.h-¹ bleeding rate, a fibrinogen infusion rate of 0.9 g.h-¹ would be required. This work supports that an individualized target-controlled fibrinogen dosing strategy is probably required to effectively correct fibrinogen levels. Integrating such models as a clinical decision support tool into a multimodal strategy that also utilizes viscoelastic testing could optimize PPH management.

papers.abstract: A meta-analysis in a recent issue of the British Journal of Anaesthesia pools randomised evidence on intraoperative arterial blood pressure targets in nine trials in noncardiac surgery. With a total of 14 658 patients included in the analysis, the authors show that higher mean arterial pressure targets do not reduce 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury, or myocardial injury. These findings reinforce the distinction between low blood pressure as a marker of perioperative vulnerability and low blood pressure as a modifiable therapeutic target. Correcting arterial pressure might normalise a number without removing the underlying physiological vulnerability that drives adverse postoperative outcomes. Therefore, this meta-analysis supports a shift from reflexive increases in blood pressure targets towards attention to the underlying cause of haemodynamic instability.

papers.abstract: T cell senescence is an important dysfunctional state associated with tumor progression, but whether senescent T (Tsen) cells directly reprogram tumor cell behavior remains unknown. Here, single-cell transcriptomic analyses identify abundant Tsen cells across breast, colorectal, and lung cancers. Tsen cells actively promote tumor growth, metastasis, stemness, and chemotherapy resistance by reprogramming tumor cells in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, lipid-enriched senescence-associated secretory phenotypes (SASPs) from Tsen cells drive metabolic remodeling and activate STAT1/STAT3 signaling in tumor cells, establishing a pro-tumorigenic state. Therapeutically, depletion of Tsen cells or disruption of tumor lipid metabolic reprogramming suppresses Tsen-mediated tumor progression and metastasis in vivo. Our findings establish Tsen cells as active orchestrators of tumor cell biological functions through lipid-rich SASP-dependent intercellular communication and reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking immune senescence to cancer progression. Targeting Tsen cells or their metabolic crosstalk with tumor cells can enhance anti-tumor immunity and improve therapeutic responses.

papers.abstract: Whether targeting an individualized mean arterial pressure (MAP) during cardiac surgery improves outcomes remains uncertain. The balance between improved perfusion and vasopressor-driven blood pressure augmentation is unclear. In this single-blind, multicenter randomized clinical trial conducted in 10 tertiary centers in France, adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned to either individualized MAP management (target within ±10% of preoperative baseline during surgery and for 24 h postoperatively) or standard management (target MAP ≥65 mm Hg). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute kidney injury, or prespecified neurologic complications within 7 days. Safety outcomes included hemorrhagic complications and transfusion requirements. A total of 172 patients were enrolled before the trial was stopped early by the data and safety monitoring board because of increased bleeding in the individualized group. Mean intraoperative MAP was higher with individualized management (80.6 vs 75.6 mm Hg; P<0.001), despite limited target adherence (33% of intraoperative time) and greater vasopressor use. The primary outcome occurred in 27 of 85 patients (32%) in the individualized group and 25 of 87 (29%) in the standard group (relative risk, 1.1; 95% CI, 0.7 to 1.8; P=0.76). Hemorrhagic complications occurred more frequently in the individualized group (18% vs 3%; P=0.003). In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, it was not possible to determine whether an individualized MAP strategy reduced major postoperative complications. More bleeding complications were observed in the individualized group. Future studies should further investigate this safety signal when evaluating individualized blood pressure targets.

papers.abstract: To assess the feasibility of using hypoxia-powered magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to guide prospective sampling of high-response habitats beyond contrast enhancement in glioblastoma. Nine treatment-naive patients with histologically confirmed isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-wildtype glioblastoma underwent blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) MRI during a controlled transient hypoxic stimulus on the evening before surgery. Anatomical segmentation and voxel-wise temporal decomposition generated normalized hypoxia response maps. Otsu thresholding defined a high-response habitat outside contrast enhancement. Targets were confirmed with the surgeon according to anatomical accessibility and eloquence, transferred to neuronavigation, and sampled before major debulking. We divided the specimen for formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded neuropathology and frozen-tissue storage. Neuronavigation transfer succeeded in all nine cases. Eight targets were accessible and sampled. Seven sampled targets contained tumor. One yielded reactive cortex and white matter without definite tumor. No target-sampling complications were observed among the eight sampled procedures. Hypoxia-powered MRI could be integrated into prospective neuronavigation-guided sampling beyond contrast enhancement. Tumor was identified in seven of eight sampled targets. By translating a tracer-free physiological response map into coordinate-matched tissue, the GLIOXY workflow enables prospective, targeted tissue sampling of non-enhancing glioblastoma regions.

papers.abstract: Gene expression is regulated by the targeted degradation of transcription factors through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Transcription factors destined for degradation are recognized by E3 ubiquitin-protein ligases through motifs termed degrons, embedded within the sequence. In this study, we systematically map degrons in all 1626 human transcription factors. We find thousands of both known and previously unidentified degrons and characterize their sequence properties. Active degrons placed within exposed and intrinsically disordered regions contribute to modulating the abundance of the transcription factors, while the most common somatic mutations that are linked to skin cutaneous melanoma lead to unfolding and exposure of a latent degron buried in the zinc finger structure. We present examples of compartment-specific degrons and demonstrate that variant effects in transcription factors correlate with degron potency. Last, we show that while >60% of all predicted transcriptional activation domains overlap with strong degrons, acidic residues within the remaining transactivating regions counter the degron potency, showing how degrons can shape the transcription factor sequence landscape.

papers.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma. However, it is unclear whether aging fuels tumor evolution by altering mutation rates, changing the microenvironmentally induced selection on drivers, or both. We analyzed 5472 melanomas, estimating how selection on individual variants changes with patient age while accounting for differing neutral mutation rates. Neutral mutation rates increased only modestly with age; ultraviolet damage remained predominant, but endogenous processes increasingly contributed to older tumors. In contrast, selection on major drivers was strongly age dependent: The advantage of BRAF V600E declined precipitously with age, whereas NRAS Q61 mutations gained advantage. TERT promoter mutations became more frequent, yet less advantageous. Aging therefore reshapes melanoma evolution primarily by altering selection, motivating age-conscious evaluation of clinical biomarkers and therapies.

papers.abstract: To identify the genes and pathways required for the survival of MYC -amplified cancers, we engineered an isogenic cell system in which transformation is driven by oncogenic MYC . Using a genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 library, we identified the mitochondrial membrane translocase TIMM17A as uniquely essential for the survival of MYC-transformed cells. This dependency arises from MYC-driven suppression of TIMM17B , the paralog of TIMM17A . TIMM17A/B is an essential component of the TIM23 mitochondrial protein import complex, and the MYC-induced suppression of TIMM17B creates a strong dependency on TIMM17A . N-acetylaspartate supplementation rescued TIMM17A dependency in MYC -amplified cell lines, highlighting the unique and crucial role of this metabolite in the cell fitness of MYC -amplified cancers. These observations identify a paralog dependency required for the survival of a subset of MYC-driven cancers.

papers.abstract: Genomic instability and dysregulated RNA processing are each recognized as core hallmarks of cancer, but accumulating evidence indicates that they are mechanistically intertwined rather than independent features. Chromosomal instability, mismatch-repair deficiency, and homologous recombination deficiency can reshape RNA splicing, 3' end formation, and RNA surveillance through changes in gene dosage, DNA damage signaling, and alterations in regulatory elements. Conversely, aberrant splicing, polyadenylation, and RNA modifications can impair DNA repair, perturb mitotic control, and promote replication stress, thereby reinforcing genomic instability. This bidirectional circuit drives clinically relevant phenotypes, including therapeutic resistance, immune modulation, and emergent vulnerabilities that are not captured by DNA-centric biomarkers alone. Here, we present a unified framework for the genome instability-RNA processing axis and its direct clinical implications for cancer diagnosis, treatment stratification, and therapeutic exploitation, highlighting the most actionable mechanistic interfaces and discussing how integrated DNA-RNA biomarkers and rational combination strategies could extend precision oncology beyond static genomic lesions.

papers.abstract: FOXP3-expressing regulatory T cells (Tregs) are a specialized subset of T lymphocytes that are crucial for maintaining immune homeostasis and preventing autoimmunity. However, their pervasive presence and potent immunosuppressive functions within the tumor microenvironment (TME) are a barrier to anti-tumor immunity, presenting a major challenge for cancer immunotherapy. In this review, we discuss strategies for the therapeutic modulation of Tregs. Current and emerging promising technological approaches include antibody-based approaches, small molecule inhibitors, engineered Tregs, microbiome modulation, and Treg survival manipulations. Additionally, existing and promising combinatorial therapies integrate Treg cell targeting with complementary treatment strategies. The goal of this review is to spotlight how Treg-targeted interventions can overcome immune escape and ultimately enhance immunotherapy efficacy to improve clinical outcomes in cancer patients.

papers.abstract: Long-term real-world data on Luspatercept (Luspa) in lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes with ring sideroblasts (MDS-RS) and transfusion-dependent anemia (RBC-TD) who are refractory or ineligible to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) remain limited. Despite evidence of efficacy from clinical trials and real-world studies, long-term data in routine clinical practice are scarce, particularly regarding its effects on non-erythroid lineages. Furthermore, there is currently no consensus on the total duration of treatment, especially in non-responding cases. Thus, we analyzed 48 patients with low-risk MDS-RS treated with Luspa for ESA-refractory RBC-TD. Response was assessed at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years according to International Working Group (IWG) 2018 criteria. At 6 months, 23/42 (54.8%) and 15/42 (35.7%) patients reached a response and transfusion independence, respectively. At 1 year, 16/30 (53.3%) patients showed a response, including 12 who already responded at 6 months. At 2 years, 10/20 (50%) patients maintained response and 2/20 (10%) were de novo responders. Treatment was well tolerated, with no significant adverse events reported; 21 (43.8%) patients discontinued Luspa, principally due to lack of response. After a median follow-up of 29.8 months (95% CI: 24.4-35.2), 6-month responders had longer overall survival in a landmark analysis. Exploratory analyses identified associations of 6-month response with additional somatic mutations and the SF3B1 hotspot mutation, the latter retained in the multivariable model; monocyte count was associated with 2-year response. Neutrophil counts significantly increased at 1 year compared with baseline, while platelet counts remained stable. Intriguingly, monocytes were increased at the three time points compared to baseline. Specifically, long-term responders presented higher levels of neutrophils and monocytes, as well decreased level of LDH, compared with non-responders. Responses were observed during long-term treatment, mainly in patients who had responded at earlier assessments. Decreasing evaluable sample sizes and the retrospective design limit interpretation. Associations with survival and non-erythroid blood counts require confirmation and should not be interpreted as causal effects.
