papers.abstract: Sepsis_associated encephalopathy (SAE) denotes acute cerebral dysfunction triggered by sepsis and is accompanied by high mortality. Our previous study showed that TIPE2 significantly ameliorated cognitive impairment in SAE mice by inhibiting neuroinflammation, but the specific mechanism was unknown. TIPE2 expression and cell specificity were analysed by scRNA‑seq and immunofluorescence. To establish SAE, cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) was carried out in TIPE2 knockout (KO) and WT mice. Neuronal/synaptic damage was assessed by TUNEL and TEM; cognitive function by behavioural tests and EEG. Hippocampal scRNA‑seq compared WT and TIPE2 KO mice. In vitro, primary microglia and BV2 cells were stimulated with LPS/nigericin. Protein expression (Western blot/IF), RhoA activation (GST‑pulldown), glucose/lactate levels, ROS production, and TIPE2‑RhoA interaction (Co‑IP/confocal) were examined. scRNA‑seq confirmed that TIPE2 is predominantly expressed in microglia and downregulated in SAE; its deficiency promotes pro‑inflammatory microglia associated with pyroptosis and glycolysis. TIPE2 KO significantly aggravated cognitive impairment, promoted M1 polarisation, enhanced pyroptosis (GSDMD cleavage, caspase‑1 activation), and increased ROS production. Mechanistically, TIPE2 directly bound to RhoA and inhibited its activation, thereby suppressing NLRP3‑mediated pyroptosis and glycolysis in microglia. Treatment with the RhoA‑specific inhibitor Rhosin reversed TIPE2 deficiency‑induced microglial polarisation, pyroptosis, ROS production, and glycolytic reprogramming, and also ameliorated cognitive dysfunction in TIPE2 KO mice. TIPE2 protects against SAE by directly interacting with RhoA, inhibiting its activation, and subsequently suppressing NLRP3‑mediated microglial pyroptosis and glycolysis.

papers.abstract: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is widely used for screening and diagnosis of prostate cancer (CaP). Variation in PSA levels is influenced by age, genetics and other factors, yet this variation has not been well characterized in African men. We used data on serum PSA extracted from medical records from prostate cancer cases and controls collected as part of the Men of African Descent and Carcinoma of the Prostate (MADCaP) network. We evaluate the association of PSA levels with country of origin, age, body mass index (BMI), and polygenic risk score (PRS). The median PSA levels were 41.8 (0.2-9696) ng/ml in 1,907 prostate cancer cases and 1.235 (0.01-9.72) ng/ml in 902 controls. Higher PSA levels were associated with increasing age, lower BMI, higher Gleason Score, and more advanced tumor stage in cases, explaining approximately 35% of variation in log-transformed PSA levels. In controls, 4.8% of PSA variation was explained by age. Our data in African men are consistent with non-African studies that report PSA levels increase with age, inversely with BMI (suggesting a PSA dilution effect or reverse causation), and with more aggressive disease in cases. These data may be used to help understand PSA distributions and in the future may guide screening practices in African men.

papers.abstract: Intrinsic biological processes and carcinogenic exposures leave cumulative DNA methylation (DNAme) imprints in epithelial cells. These changes reflect cellular composition, replicative/mitotic age and impaired differentiation capacity, and arise long before clinically detectable cancer, consistent with the concept of field cancerisation. Importantly, such epigenetic alterations are not confined to the tissue of origin but extend to anatomically distant epithelia that share developmental lineage and/or carcinogen exposure/susceptibility, thereby serving as field defect indicators. Notably, these signatures are dynamic and responsive to preventive interventions, enabling both risk assessment and real-time monitoring of prevention efficacy. The epithelial epigenome is thus emerging as a unified, minimally invasive platform for personalised, multi-cancer prevention.

papers.abstract: The RIG-I pathway, a key component of the innate immune system that classically detects cytosolic viral RNA, has also been implicated in regulating tumor cell viability, radiosensitivity, and patient survival across multiple cancer types. However, these effects appear to be context-dependent and partly contradictory. Whether radiotherapy modulates tumor-intrinsic RIG-I signaling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) depending on HPV status, and whether such modulation is associated with changes in the tumor immune phenotype, remains unknown. Four human HNSCC cell lines (two HPV-negative and two HPV-positive), along with siRNA-mediated RIG-I knockdown and a CRISPR/Cas9-generated RIG-I knockout derivative, were treated with radiotherapy. Tumor cells were analyzed for their immune phenotype, including RIG-I expression via Western blot and flow cytometry, IFN-β secretion via ELISA, and PD-L1 and PD-L2 expression via flow cytometry. Radiotherapy, dose- and fraction-dependent, induced the upregulation of RIG-I expression and IFN-β secretion from HPV-negative HNSCC cells. The knockdown and knockout of the RIG-I-encoding gene DDX58 in the HPV-negative cell line HSC4 minimized both IFN-β secretion and PD-L1 and PD-L2 expression. These effects could be replicated by pre-exposing HPV-negative cell lines to the RIG-I inhibitor RIG012 before irradiation. Interestingly, HPV-positive cells showed less radiotherapy-mediated modulation of RIG-I and of the tumor cell phenotype of immune-related surface markers and showed no significant reaction to the inhibitor treatment. The previously unrecognized RIG-I-IFN-β axis is a central regulator of RT-induced immune checkpoint modulation for HPV-negative HNSCC. These results provide new opportunities to reshape the immune response following RT in HNSCC.

papers.abstract: Early and continuous antiretroviral therapy (ART) reduces cancer risk in people with HIV (PWH), yet residual risk potentially driven by persistent B-cell activation remains. We used observational and genetic triangulation to evaluate whether baseline B-cell biomarkers are associated with subsequent cancer risk. We conducted: (i) a nested case-control study within the INSIGHT trials (158 cases and 313 matched controls) assessing B-cell biomarkers (sCD23, sCD27, sCD30, CXCL13) in PWH; and (ii) two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to evaluate likely causal relationships between these proteins and 23 cancer types using general-population genome-wide association studies. Median time from study entry to cancer diagnosis was 2.9 years. In PWH, CXCL13 was associated with overall cancer risk (highest tertile vs. lowest tertile OR 2.36, 95% CI 1.24-4.5), driven by infection-related cancers (N = 82; OR 4.81, 1.76-13.1) and lymphoma (N = 36; OR 9.92, 1.58-62.2). The CXCL13 association remained robust among virally suppressed participants (P = 0.018). sCD30 was also associated with infection-related cancers (OR 2.77, 1.09-7.03). sCD23 showed a linear association with infection-related cancer (OR per SD 1.42, 1.01-2.00), though tertile-based analyses were non-significant. In the general population, MR meta-analyses showed null associations for these biomarkers across 23 cancer types (P > 0.05). Our study links B-cell markers with cancer risk in PWH, identifying CXCL13 as a marker of infection-related cancer risk despite effective ART, highlighting a "residual inflammatory gap" for modern risk stratification. The lack of causal MR signals suggests these proteins are markers of HIV-associated immune activation rather than universal etiological factors for cancer.

papers.abstract: JAK1 signaling supports a suppressive tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) state and may also promote tumor-intrinsic oncogenic signaling. Leiomyosarcoma (LMS) is a soft tissue sarcoma (STS) subtype known to have abundant TAM infiltration, which is often polarized to an immunosuppressive M2 phenotype and contributes to immune evasion. We hypothesized that using a JAK1 inhibitor could alter TAM phenotypes in the LMS tumor microenvironment (TME), helping patients and potentially enabling future combination studies. Here, we present results from a pilot study of itacitinib, a JAK1 inhibitor, for LMS. We analyzed patients in the LMS cohort of a pilot study of the selective JAK1 inhibitor itacitinib (started at 300 mg daily in 28-day cycles) (NCT03670069). Serial tumor biopsies and peripheral blood samples were collected for correlative analysis. Despite the heavily pretreated LMS population, PFS rate at 3 and 6 months for LMS was 75% (95% CI: 50%-100%) and 25% (95% CI: 5%-100%), respectively, and the median OS was 101 weeks (range: 70-256). Six of eight patients with LMS achieved stable disease. Serial biopsies demonstrated a decrease in M2 TAM but without a corresponding inflammatory response and with a decrease of inflammatory infiltrates, suggesting that JAK1 inhibition may have direct anti-tumor effects in this subtype and that the impacts of the TAM reduction may be related to their tumor supportive and angiogenic functions, rather than immune inhibitory functions. These data support further investigation of JAK1 inhibition in LMS as part of rational immunotherapeutic combinations.

papers.abstract: Accurate endotracheal tube (ETT) sizing is essential in pediatric airway management to optimize ventilation and reduce complications. Traditional methods, including age-based formulas and distal phalanx width (DPW), may lack precision. Subglottic ultrasound (US) has emerged as a promising tool, but its predictive accuracy compared with DPW remains unclear. This study aimed to compare accuracy, agreement, diagnostic performance, and clinical applicability of subglottic US versus DPW for predicting optimal ETT size in children, while recognizing that the enrolled cohort was predominantly school-aged. In this prospective observational study, pediatric patients aged 0-12 years undergoing elective or emergency intubation were assessed. Pre-intubation measurements included subglottic transverse airway diameter by ultrasound (ACUSON Juniper, microconvex probe, 5-10 MHz) and DPW by digital calipers. Predicted ETT sizes were compared with the final clinically accepted cuffed ETT inner diameter confirmed by leak testing and cuff pressure optimization. Agreement was evaluated using Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients, while diagnostic performance was defined a priori as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), likelihood ratios, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Logistic regression identified predictors of good ETT fit. Among 160 patients, the median age was 8.8 years (IQR 7.0-10.5), indicating predominance of older children. Ultrasound-predicted ETT size showed a stronger correlation with actual size (r = 0.479, p < 0.001) than DPW (r = 0.248, p = 0.002). Ultrasound predictions had narrower Bland-Altman limits of agreement, although ultrasound measurement is operator-dependent. DPW showed poor sensitivity (5.9%) but high specificity (99.3%) for identifying underfit ETTs, with limited overall discrimination (ROC AUC = 0.53). Only subglottic diameter was a significant predictor of good ETT fit. Subglottic ultrasound showed better agreement with clinically accepted ETT size than DPW in this predominantly school-aged pediatric cohort. These findings support the potential role of ultrasound as an adjunct to pediatric airway assessment, but conclusions should be interpreted cautiously in infants and younger children because they were under-represented. Standardized measurement protocols and operator training are needed before broad implementation.

papers.abstract: With 2 million new cases annually, lung cancer is among the most frequent and the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Incidence trends differ by gender, decreasing in men but increasing in women, partly due to later tobacco uptake. However, biological differences may also contribute, including the potential role of estrogen exposure. This study aimed to investigate the influence of lifetime hormonal exposure on lung cancer risk in women. WELCA is a multicenter population-based case-control study conducted in Ile-de-France between 2014 and 2017 among women aged 18-75 years. The study included 716 cases of incident primary lung cancer and 756 controls frequency-matched by age and area of residence. Information was collected through standardized questionnaires on lifestyle factors, occupational history, reproductive history, and use of exogenous hormones. Odds-ratios (OR) and confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using multivariable logistic regression models. A later age at last pregnancy (≥ 33 vs. ≤ 28 years) and ever use of hormonal contraceptives was associated with a lower risk of lung cancer (OR = 0.60; 0.42-0.85 and OR = 0.57; 0.39-0.84, respectively). However, a later age at cessation of the pill use was associated with an increased risk (≥ 39 vs. ≤ 30 years: OR = 1.46; 1.06-2.03). Finally, a longer reproductive lifespan was inversely associated with lung cancer (≥ 39 vs. ≤ 36 years: OR = 0.69; 0.50-0.95). These findings suggest lifetime hormonal exposure may influence lung cancer risk in women. They support the hypothesis of a hormonally mediated pathway and highlight the need for further studies on sex-specific lung cancer risk.

papers.abstract: To evaluate whether the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade modifies the association of combined locoregional plus systemic therapy versus systemic therapy alone with outcomes in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This multicente retrospective study enrolled 525 patients, stratified by the established ALBI grade cut-off into ALBI-low (Grade 1, ALBI score ≤ -2.60, n = 257) and ALBI-high (Grade 2/3, n = 268). Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed in the whole cohort and within each ALBI stratum; survival, tumor response, and safety were compared in matched cohorts, with effect modification tested by a treatment × ALBI interaction term. After PSM, combination therapy was associated with better overall survival (OS) (hazard ratio [HR] 0.51, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.34-0.76; p = 0.001) and progression-free survival (PFS) (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56-0.96; p = 0.024). The association was observed in ALBI-low patients (OS: HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.18-0.56, p < 0.001; PFS: HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.41-0.85, p = 0.004), who also had higher objective response rates by modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST; 70.9% vs. 38.8%, p < 0.001) and RECIST 1.1 (55.3% vs. 30.1%, p < 0.001). No significant association was seen in ALBI-high patients (OS: HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.47-1.45, p = 0.504; PFS: HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.71-1.58, p = 0.792), and the treatment × ALBI interaction was significant for OS (p = 0.019) and PFS (p = 0.035). Overall and Grade 3-4 adverse reactions were comparable, but elevated bilirubin (33.0% vs. 17.0%, p = 0.012) and transaminases (35.1% vs. 20.2%, p = 0.022) were more frequent with combination therapy in the ALBI-high cohort. In this multicenter real-world cohort, combination therapy was associated with better outcomes in patients of ALBI Grade 1 but not Grade 2/3, in whom hepatic toxicity was more frequent, and the exploratory treatment × ALBI interaction was significant. ALBI grade may help identify patients more likely to benefit from combined locoregional and systemic therapy, although prospective validation is required.

papers.abstract: Multicancer early detection tests could be used for cancer screening, but may lead to harms, including false positive results and overdiagnosis of indolent tumors that would not have become clinically evident during that person's lifetime. We assessed the potential for these screening harms in the context of future population-based screening with a multicancer early detection test. We used a microsimulation model to assess potential population-level impacts of screening at ages 50-75 years with a multicancer early detection test in Canada. We assumed high test specificity (97%-99.1%) and test sensitivity increasing with cancer stage. The model includes latent indolent cancers that would not be diagnosed within that person's lifetime but can be overdiagnosed through screen-detection. We calculated the yearly and cumulative lifetime probabilities of screening overdiagnosis and false positive test results, assuming a range of preclinical screen-detectable periods (2-5 years). An estimated 2.1%-6.0% of all yearly screen-detected cancers with a multicancer screening test were predicted to be overdiagnoses across scenarios. The proportion of overdiagnosis varied by site and strongly increased with age, going from 1% at age 50 to over 10% of screen-detected cancers by age 75. The test positive predictive value ranged from 15.9% to 77.6%, meaning that there could be 0.3-5.3 false positives with no underlying cancer for every true cancer case detected by the test. Population-level multicancer screening with a multicancer early detection test would lead to screen-related overdiagnosis; healthcare systems should consider how overdiagnoses and screening false positives may increase their follow-up capacity and caseload.

papers.abstract: Recurrence in oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) remains a prognostic challenge, which necessitates additional prognostic approaches reflecting tumor biology. Therefore, we developed an objective, observer-independent, multiparametric model incorporating features of the tumoral and stromal compartments. Digitized whole-slide images from 80 patients with TSCC were analyzed using a combination of semi-automatic and deep learning-based approaches. We extracted quantitative histomorphological features, including tumor/stroma ratio (TSR), lymphocyte/stromal cell ratio in the tumor stroma (LSCR), and the modified Polsby-Popper (MPP) score reflecting tumor disjointedness. Human trophoblast cell surface glycoprotein (Trop-2) expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry in central and invasive-front tumor regions sampled via tissue microarrays (TMA) and quantified using the H-score. A composite score (CS) was constructed by summing points from these parameters; as Trop-2 did not improve cross-validated discrimination, a final three-marker CS (TSR, LSCR, MPP) was adopted as the final model. Patients were stratified into prognostic groups and recurrence-free survival (RFS) was analyzed. While individual parameters showed only trends, the CS stratified patients into poor, intermediate and favorable prognosis groups with 5-year RFS probabilities of 64.6%, 75.3%, and 100.0%. Repeated five-fold cross-validation yielded a cross-fitted consensus concordance index of 0.587 (mean per-repetition concordance index 0.567 ± 0.039), compared with an apparent concordance index of 0.676, with no evidence of a difference from conventional prognostic factors. In exploratory multivariable Firth-penalized Cox regression adjusted for pT3-pT4a category, the favorable group showed a lower recurrence hazard than the poor group (HR 0.104, 95% CI 0.001-0.854, p = 0.0316); this non-cross-validated estimate is fragile given the small favorable group without recurrence events. This observer-independent whole-slide image approach may provide complementary prognostic information to conventional histological features but requires external validation.

papers.abstract: Patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) who develop resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy experience significantly poorer outcomes and shorter progression-free survival (PFS). This study evaluates whether pretreatment CT-based abdominal body composition is associated with platinum resistance and PFS, and whether its incorporation alongside clinical variables improves prognostic model performance. This retrospective study included 321 patients with HGSOC (mean age 65 ± 10 years; 28.0% platinum-resistant) treated with platinum-based chemotherapy between 2011 and 2023. Deep learning algorithms quantified abdominal body composition features from pretreatment CT scans, including skeletal muscle, bone, subcutaneous (SAT), visceral (VAT), and intramuscular (IMAT) adipose tissues. Platinum resistance, defined as disease progression during therapy or within 6 months of the final infusion, was the primary outcome. PFS was analyzed as a secondary outcome using Cox proportional hazards modeling. Analyses were stratified by chemotherapy sequence (neoadjuvant vs. adjuvant). Survival models incorporating clinical and CT-derived features were evaluated using 10-fold cross-validated time-dependent AUC over a 5-year follow-up window to predict PFS. External validation was partially performed in an independent cohort of 58 patients with HGSOC. Increased SAT and IMAT and decreased skeletal muscle density were independently associated with platinum resistance, with high SAT remaining significant in both the internal and external cohorts (p < 0.05). High adiposity and low muscle density were similarly associated with shorter PFS. Survival models combining clinical and CT-derived features consistently outperformed clinical-only models across all evaluated model classes. The Elastic Net Cox regression model incorporating both feature sets achieved the highest AUC of 0.704 (95% CI: 0.660-0.748). Pretreatment CT-derived abdominal body composition is independently associated with platinum resistance and PFS in HGSOC, and its incorporation into predictive clinical models improves discrimination. Body composition assessment may help identify patients at increased risk of platinum resistance and early disease progression.

papers.abstract: Primary-tumor major pathological response (MPR) and postoperative nodal status are both used to assess response after neoadjuvant therapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but discordant response after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy is poorly characterized. We evaluated a combined primary tumor-lymph node (PT-LN) framework for risk stratification. This retrospective single-center cohort included patients treated with two cycles of paclitaxel, cisplatin, and camrelizumab followed by curative-intent surgery between January 2019 and December 2024. Among 414 screened patients, 367 were included. MPR was defined as 10% or less residual viable tumor cells in the primary tumor. Patients were classified as PT-MPR/ypN0, PT-MPR/ypN+, PT-non-MPR/ypN0, or PT-non-MPR/ypN+. Disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), first documented recurrence, and pathological model performance were evaluated. Sixty-nine patients (18.8%) had PT-MPR/ypN+ disease. DFS and OS differed across groups (both overall log-rank p < 0.001). Compared with PT-MPR/ypN0, PT-MPR/ypN+ was associated with worse DFS (baseline-adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 5.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.82-12.14) and OS (HR, 18.06; 95% CI, 5.53-59.06; both p < 0.001), with similar conclusions after additional pathological adjustment. Regional lymph node recurrence occurred in 44.9% of PT-MPR/ypN+ patients versus 3.6%, 6.7%, and 16.7% in the other groups (global p < 0.001). The combined PT-LN framework had 3-year DFS and OS AUCs of 0.798 and 0.818, with modest gains over LN-only classification. Residual nodal disease despite primary-tumor MPR identifies an adverse phenotype with predominantly regional nodal recurrence. The combined framework is an interpretable stratification approach requiring external validation; surveillance and treatment implications remain hypothesis-generating.

papers.abstract: Restarting immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) after an immune-related adverse event (irAE) requires balancing toxicity against antitumor benefit. Prior reviews often mixed post-irAE restart with retreatment after progression or combined cohorts with case reports. This systematic review evaluated cohort evidence on ICI restart after irAE-related interruption. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, CENTRAL, and reference lists were searched through 24 April 2026 for observational clinical cohort studies. Primary outcomes were index-irAE recurrence, any post-rechallenge irAE (recurrent or new), and grade ≥ 3 post-rechallenge irAE (recurrent or new). Secondary outcomes included toxicity-related discontinuation, objective response, disease control, overall survival, and progression-free survival. Thirty-five cohorts comprising 1551 rechallenged patients were included; endpoint-specific denominators varied. Index-irAE recurrence was 25.4% (95% confidence interval [CI], 21.4-29.7; 30 studies). Any post-rechallenge irAE (recurrent or new) was 44.2% (95% CI, 37.8-50.8; 23 studies). Grade ≥ 3 post-rechallenge irAE (recurrent or new) was 19.8% (95% CI, 15.3-25.1; 22 studies). Toxicity-related discontinuation was 25.3%. Pooled objective response and disease control were 44.3% and 72.7%, respectively. Survival data were available from nine studies for overall survival and four studies for progression-free survival. Hazard ratios were displayed individually, and no summary hazard ratio was calculated. ICI rechallenge after irAE-related interruption was accompanied by frequent post-rechallenge toxicity, while objective response and disease control remained evident after treatment resumption. These estimates inform individualized risk-benefit assessment and identify irAE phenotype, recovery status, and rechallenge strategy as priorities for prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract: Phase III clinical trials offer patients access to emerging therapies, yet geographical access varies significantly. The profile of research facilities conducting such trials can provide insights into global disparities. We extracted all research sites within recruiting Phase III cancer interventional trials from the ClinicalTrials.gov database on July 23, 2024. Address components were combined and queried through the Google Maps API for standardized identification. We compared research facilities' number, density (per 1 M people), and portfolio of trials across World Bank regions and estimated the elasticity coefficient [β] of trials and research facilities per country with log-log linear models. Of 77,625 listed sites from 1287 trials, 64,018 (82.5%) were mapped to 6634 unique research facilities across 84 countries. The number of research facilities and trials by country were strongly correlated (R2 = 0.86, p value 93%, p value 90%, p value 80%, p value < 0.001). The number of research facilities is strongly associated with the volume of cancer trials across countries. Outside HICs, research facilities were less numerous, focused on systemic therapies, and frequently reliant on industry-sponsored, multiregional trials.

papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded treatment options across multiple malignancies, but their clinical benefit remains constrained by heterogeneous and sometimes serious toxicities. These toxicities rarely arise from a single component; instead, they reflect the association between target biology, molecular architecture, systemic exposure, and tissue susceptibility. We first examine the structural basis of ADC toxicity by discussing the distinct contributions of the antibody-target axis, linker, payload, drug loading, and conjugation strategy to systemic exposure and tissue toxicity. We distinguish organ-selective "on-target, off-tumor" injury from target-independent toxicity and further characterize two major off-target routes: context-dependent uptake of intact ADCs through Fcγ receptor-mediated or pinocytosis-dominant pathways, and spatially distinct exposure to released payload arising from premature systemic release or localized bystander diffusion. Furthermore, we summarize a multidisciplinary management framework, ranging from prophylactic measures to graded interventions across complex scenarios such as treatment rechallenge and combination therapy. Finally, we discuss strategies to widen the therapeutic window through exposure-response-guided dosing, next-generation molecular engineering, and emerging conjugate platforms. Artificial intelligence and computational approaches may further extend safety optimization from drug design to patient stratification and real-world surveillance. By linking molecular design, spatial exposure, and clinical management, this review provides an integrated framework to improve ADC safety while preserving antitumor efficacy.

papers.abstract: Accurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) could facilitate more individualized axillary management in breast cancer by improving identification of patients at lower risk of nodal involvement while maintaining appropriate staging for those at higher risk. Yet, reliable molecular predictors of LNM remain lacking. VEGF-C, a key driver of lymphangiogenesis, is expressed in both cancer cell and stromal compartments, but its clinical utility is unclear. In a prospectively enrolled cohort, we assessed stromal and cancer cell VEGF-C expression by immunohistochemistry using both manual scoring and a novel automated image analysis script enabling objective, reproducible classification of stromal versus epithelial cells at scale. Stromal VEGF-C was independently associated with LNM after adjustment for established predictors (P = 0.004), with prediction models reaching AUCs of up to 0.784. Cancer cell VEGF-C added no predictive value. In exploratory analyses, stromal VEGF-C provided predictive information comparable to that of vascular invasion, a strong predictor of LNM that is generally unavailable preoperatively. These findings identify stromal VEGF-C as a potential preoperative biomarker for nodal risk stratification. However, given the observational and predictive nature of the present study, stromal VEGF-C should be considered complementary to, rather than a replacement for, established pathological predictors. Its potential contribution to future axillary surgery de-escalation strategies warrants prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains a significant clinical challenge due to the emergence of drug resistance, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Aberrant regulation of the proteome drives cancer progression, and dissecting these alterations offers opportunities for targeted intervention. We aimed to identify candidate kinase dependencies in mCRC and to test a rational combination strategy in patient-derived models. We performed proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiling of 10 mCRC tissues, their matched patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and normal colon mucosa, integrated with whole-exome sequencing. Kinase activities were inferred by kinase-substrate enrichment analysis. Silmitasertib-mediated casein kinase II (CKII) inhibition, alone and combined with the MEK inhibitor trametinib, was evaluated by ex vivo drug screening, western blot, flow cytometry and drug-interaction analysis across the PDO cohort and in normal colon PDOs. PDOs recapitulated the molecular features of matched tumours. Both tissues and PDOs showed consistently elevated CKII activity. Silmitasertib exerted heterogeneous antitumour activity, and resistance was associated with MAPK and Akt-mTOR signalling activity. Combining silmitasertib with trametinib produced an additive reduction of both resistance-associated pathways with little effect on the viability of normal colon PDOs. The combination also significantly reduced CKII activity, the abundance of active β-catenin and the colorectal cancer stem cell pool. Phosphoproteomic profiling identified CKII as a therapeutic vulnerability in mCRC and provided a rationale for combining silmitasertib with MEK inhibition, offering a candidate combination strategy for mCRC.

papers.abstract: Enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis (ETBF) is a pro-carcinogenic pathobiont thought to drive oncogenesis solely through E-cadherin cleavage by its metalloprotease toxin, Bacteroides fragilis toxin (BFT). This canonical framework leaves three paradoxes unresolved: the cell type selectivity of BFT, the cytosolic engagement of NOD1 by an extracellularly secreted toxin, and the divergent epidemiology of BFT isoforms. The recent identification of claudin-4 as the obligate BFT receptor resolves the first but sharpens the others. Here we propose an outer membrane vesicle (OMV)-associated two-track model. In Track 1, the surface program, claudin-4-dependent docking drives E-cadherin ectodomain cleavage, junctional disruption and β-catenin/Th17-driven inflammation. In Track 2, the proposed intracellular program, OMV-mediated endocytosis delivers OMV-anchored BFT-1 into the endocytic compartment, where endosomal escape would permit cytosolic NOD1 engagement and activation of a GAK-NUMB-NOTCH1-HEY1 axis linked to cancer stem cell expansion and chemoresistance-an axis so far demonstrated in breast cancer cells, not in colonic epithelium. We further hypothesize an intrinsic isoform bias: BFT-2 toward surface cleavage, BFT-1 toward intracellular NOD1 engagement. This spatially resolved model unifies recent mechanistic advances with unexplained epidemiological patterns.

papers.abstract: Chemoresistance remains a major challenge in the treatment of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, the mechanisms underlying chemoresistance remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified that higher levels of Rhomboid-Like 2 (RHBDL2) expression were associated with chemoresistance and poor prognosis in patients with TNBC. Notably, the knockdown of RHBDL2 suppressed cancer stemness and chemoresistance by inhibiting CD44+/CD24- breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs) in TNBC cells. RNA sequencing analysis revealed that the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/mTOR/c-MYC signaling pathway was involved in this process. Mechanistically, we observed that RHBDL2 activated the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/mTOR/c-MYC signaling pathway by binding to EGFR. Knockdown of RHBDL2 inhibited the expression of EGFR on the TNBC cell membrane, thereby deactivating the downstream signaling pathway, and ultimately inhibiting TNBC progression and chemoresistance. Remarkably, our in vivo experiments demonstrated that knockdown of RHBDL2 effectively inhibited tumor growth in xenograft tumor models. Collectively, our study uncovers the roles and mechanisms of RHBDL2 in TNBC chemoresistance and proposes targeting RHBDL2 as an innovative therapeutic strategy to overcome chemoresistance in TNBC.

papers.abstract: Text message reminders (TMRs) and patient navigation (PN) increase bowel cancer screening uptake. To date, no studies have directly compared these interventions with one another. We conducted a three-arm randomised controlled trial with individuals, in London, who had not completed bowel cancer screening within 18 weeks of invitation. Participants were randomised to receive no reminder (usual care), TMRs at 19, 21, 23 and 25 weeks, or a TMR at 19 weeks, with telephone PN at 21, 23 and 25 weeks. The primary outcome was participation within 26 weeks of invitation. Differences were assessed using logistic regression. On an intention-to-treat basis (n = 3129), uptake was higher in the TMR and PN groups, compared with usual care (6.5% vs. 2.0%, p < 0.001; 7.5% vs. 2.0%, p < 0.001). There was no significant difference between TMR and PN groups. In the per-protocol analysis (n = 2294), uptake was significantly higher in the PN group than the TMR group (8.6 vs. 12.6%, p < 0.025). Subgroup analyses revealed telephone PN was significantly more effective than TMRs for men, specifically (14.5% vs. 6.7%, p < 0.001). While TMRs are no more effective than PN in general, implementing PN could help reduce disparities in uptake between men and women. ISRCTN17245519.

papers.abstract: Analyses disentangling the role of the gut microbiome in linking lifestyle factors to health outcomes remain limited. Here, using fecal shotgun metagenomics from 6,803 adults in the Japanese 4D cohort, we identified two opposing microbiome-mediated axes linking lifestyle to health and 15 diseases. A health-associated axis enriched in microbial metabolism of dietary components was linked to plant-based, soy and dairy intake. In contrast, a disease-associated axis, enriched in oral-derived bacteria and pathobionts, was linked to refined carbohydrates and sedentary behavior. Starter culture microorganisms used to ferment foods did not show statistically significant mediation of the observed health effects. Alcohol was associated with both health- and disease-oriented mediation patterns involving microbial host-glycan utilization. Microbiome-defined health- and disease-oriented mediator axes were supported by fecal short-chain fatty acids and plasma cytokines from >1,700 individuals, revealing butyrate-associated anti-inflammatory and pro-inflammatory host profiles, respectively. Microbiome-based prediction (MADE) scores captured lifestyle-microbiome-disease mediation patterns and distinguished individual diseases across 13 independent external cohorts from the United States, China, Sweden, Russia and Australia. We identify the gut microbiome as a key mediator linking lifestyle to health and disease, providing a framework for microbiome-based assessment to guide lifestyle interventions for health promotion and disease prevention.

papers.abstract: Adoptive chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapies have limited efficacy in solid tumors because of poor infiltration and impaired effector function, whereas radiotherapy is constrained by radioresistance and metastatic spread. Here we show that integrating the spatial precision of ionizing radiation with the biological specificity of CAR-T cells enables localized delivery of the inflammatory cytokine tumor necrosis factor (TNF). We identified radiation-responsive genes in tumor-infiltrating T cells and engineered synthetic radioinducible promoters to drive TNF expression. Human CAR-T cells carrying this construct (riTNF CAR-T cells) secreted high levels of TNF upon irradiation, independently of antigen engagement. In human xenograft and murine tumor models, the combination of riTNF CAR-T cells and local irradiation produced greater tumor regression than either treatment alone or standard CAR-T cells with irradiation. This response was associated with high intratumoral, but not systemic, TNF levels, increased tumor necrosis and apoptosis, vascular disruption and greater CAR-T cell infiltration. These findings establish a platform for spatially and temporally controlled cytokine delivery from engineered CAR-T cells.

papers.abstract: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets. Across sequencing-based and imaging-based datasets, DIRAC identified a new microvascular proliferation domain in glioblastoma, corrected cortical-layer annotations in severe Alzheimer's disease, resolved subtle structures in mouse embryos and remained robust to missing data and unseen cell types. We generated mouse spleen and thymus Stereo-CITE-seq data and used DIRAC to reveal thymic T cell migration and splenic immune cell interactions. DIRAC is fast and scales to millions of cells.

papers.abstract: Single-cell T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing enables simultaneous profiling of gene expression and TCR sequences, providing a coregistered measure of T cell phenotypic diversity and clonal dynamics. However, principled probabilistic frameworks for joint modeling of clonotype and phenotype have remained limited. Here we introduce TCRi, a hierarchical Bayesian information-theoretic framework that infers the joint probability distribution between genetic clonotype and transcriptional phenotype from paired single-cell transcriptomic and TCR sequencing data. TCRi treats phenotype assignment as a probabilistic inference problem: a variational autoencoder embeds single-cell expression into a structured latent space, and a hierarchical Bayesian model learns clonotype-specific phenotype distributions through principled information-sharing across clonotypes, patients and covariates. From these distributions, TCRi computes information-theoretic quantities: clonotypic entropy, phenotypic entropy, phenotypic flux and mutual information between clonotype and phenotype. When TCRi was applied to four real-world datasets comprising 167,118 CD8 T cells from patients with cancer treated with anti-PD-(L)1 immune checkpoint blockade, mutual information emerged as a robust discriminator of therapeutic response.

papers.abstract: Spatial omics enable the in situ characterization of tissue architecture by measuring molecular modalities. However, integrating these datasets remains challenging due to differences in spatial resolution, cross-modal alignment and molecular coverage. Here we show that Cross-scale spatial Omics Registration and Analysis via graph Learning (CORAL), a probabilistic deep generative model, leverages graph attention to integrate diverse spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic and epigenomic data across spatial scales. CORAL jointly models high-resolution datasets with limited molecular coverage and low-resolution genome-wide datasets, generating unified representations with broad molecular coverage and high spatial resolution. Across synthetic and experimental datasets from diverse tissues and platforms, CORAL accurately identifies spatial domains, predicts high-resolution molecular profiles, detects spatially variable genes and infers cell-cell interactions. Applied to spatial transcriptomic and proteomic data from hepatocellular carcinoma patients before and after immunotherapy, CORAL identified organized immune-cell subsets and signaling pathways associated with therapeutic resistance. These results demonstrate CORAL's broad applicability for resolving tissue organization and clinically relevant multicellular interactions.

papers.abstract: We aimed to evaluate and report a protocol for video double-lumen tube (VDLT) intubation in a modified lateral position and evaluate whether it shortens in-room to cut time (IRCT; defined as the time from patient entry to incision) compared with conventional supine intubation in patients undergoing elective unilateral video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). We conducted a single-centre, prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled superiority trial at a tertiary university hospital in Xi'an, China. We enrolled adults aged 18-75 yr (American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status I-III) scheduled for elective unilateral VATS requiring VDLT intubation; exclusions included body mass index > 30 kg·m-2, mouth opening < 3 cm, Mallampati class 3-4, or anticipated difficult airway. Participants were randomized 1:1 to modified-lateral-position (Group L) or supine-position (Group S) VDLT intubation using a computer-generated sequence with sealed-envelope allocation concealment. Operators were unblinded; nonoperator staff collecting postoperative data and the outcome analyst were blinded to allocation. The primary outcome was IRCT. Sixty-two patients were randomized (Group L, N = 31; Group S, N = 31), and all were analyzed for the primary outcome. Mean (standard deviation [SD]) IRCT was shorter in Group L (18.1 [2.0] min) than in Group S (31.1 [3.3] min), with a mean difference (L-S) of -13.0 min (95% confidence interval [CI], -14.4 to -11.6; P < 0.001). Intubation time was similar (mean [SD], 103 [15] sec vs 97 [15] sec; P = 0.10). Video double-lumen tube malpositioning occurred in 1/31 (3%) cases in Group L vs 15/31 (48%) cases in Group S (relative risk [RR], 0.067; 95% CI, 0.009 to 0.474; P < 0.001). Sore throat within 48 h occurred in 9/31 (29%) patients in Group L vs 18/31 (58%) patients in Group S (RR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.27 to 0.94; P = 0.02). In patients undergoing unilateral VATS, VDLT intubation in a modified lateral position shortened IRCT. In exploratory analyses, several secondary outcomes favoured this approach. Intubation in a modified lateral position may be a feasible alternative to conventional supine position intubation in these patients. ChiCTR.org.cn ( ChiCTR2500112254 ); first posted 21 October 2025.

papers.abstract: We report the results of a Phase I trial of intravenous (IV) vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) engineered to express human interferon beta (hIFNβ) and thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) in patients with stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (EC). Eligible patients with stage IV or recurrent EC with largest tumor diameter ≤ 5 cm were enrolled and received a single IV infusion of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS in a standard '3 + 3' dose escalation. Five dose-levels were planned. Primary endpoint was determination of the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, tumor response, and immune correlates. An exploratory post-hoc analysis evaluated clinical responses to subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies. From 9/15/2017-1/10/23, 21 eligible patients were treated. One patient at DL2 experienced grade 3 dehydration associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and one experienced transient grade 4 asymptomatic lymphopenia, prompting protocol modification of the DLT definition. One of six patients at DL4 experienced grade 3 delirium meeting DLT criteria. Dose escalation to DL5 was not feasible because of investigational agent production limitations; MTD was not reached. The most common treatment related AEs were transient hematologic toxicities, liver enzyme elevations, and CRS. At day 29, 8 patients had progressive disease (PD); 1 entered hospice due to PD before day 29. Two patients had stable disease for at least 6 months following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS. Of the 15 patients who received subsequent ICI-based therapy following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, 4 had durable SD with a median follow up of 40.4 (95% CI 30.4-not reached) months. IV VSV-hIFNβ-NIS had an acceptable safety profile in patients with advanced or recurrent EC. Further investigation of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, particularly in combination with immune checkpoint blockade, is warranted.

papers.abstract: Somatic variant detection is technically challenging due to low variant allele fractions, the confounding presence of germline variation, and reference bias. Linear references, such as GRCh38, miss sample-specific variation, leading to misalignments and incorrect variant calls. Although telomere-to-telomere donor-specific assemblies (DSAs) accurately represent individual genomes, their application is limited by cost and technical barriers. Alternatively, the graph-based human pangenome provides a scalable framework to improve read alignment and perform genome inference. Here, we benchmarked somatic variant detection using GRCh38, graph-based pangenomes, and pangenome-inferred DSAs with a HapMap mixture dataset and the COLO829 melanoma cell line. Pangenome-guided alignment improves read mapping and somatic variant calling accuracy. Furthermore, personalized pangenomes partially reconstruct donor-specific genomic content, improving accuracy, reducing germline contamination, and enabling detection of events in loci absent or poorly represented in GRCh38. These findings demonstrate that graph-based and personalized pangenomes are effective strategies for enhancing somatic variant detection compared with GRCh38.

papers.abstract: Uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) maintains a poor prognosis due to its aggressive behavior and limited therapeutic response. Preclinical progress is severely hindered by traditional subcutaneous models that often fail to metastasize, despite one-third of uLMS patients displaying metastases at diagnosis. This study aimed to establish a reproducible, physiologically accurate orthotopic uLMS murine model that faithfully recapitulates disease progression and chemotherapeutic response. Primary subcutaneous tumors were established via SK-LMS-1 cell injections in NOD/SCID mice. Harvested xenografts were surgically implanted heterotopically (subcutaneous flank) or orthotopically (uterine myometrium). Eight days post-implantation, mice were randomized to receive intraperitoneal doxorubicin (1.2 mg/kg twice weekly) or vehicle control for 3 weeks. Tumor growth was tracked longitudinally via MRI (orthotopic) or caliper measurement (subcutaneous). Immunohistochemistry evaluated tumor vitality, microenvironment hypoxia, vascular density, and metastatic spread. Orthotopic tumors exhibited significantly accelerated growth kinetics compared to subcutaneous counterparts. This expansion was supported by co-option of host uterine vasculature, resulting in ample tumor perfusion, suppressed tissue hypoxia, and robust proliferation. Crucially, 37% of primary orthotopic tumors developed spontaneous, multi-organ metastases to pulmonary, omental, and intraperitoneal sites by 4 weeks. Orthotopic tumors demonstrated heightened sensitivity to doxorubicin, achieving a 55% volume reduction compared to 44% in subcutaneous controls, mediated by superior intratumoral drug delivery supported by increased cleaved caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. Surgical orthotopic xenografting recapitulates clinical uLMS, demonstrating site-dependent vascular co-option, spontaneous systemic metastasis, and enhanced chemosensitivity. By mimicking physiological characteristics of human uLMS, this orthotopic model offers significant potential for enhancing understanding of uLMS and evaluating novel therapies.

papers.abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapy is a cornerstone of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) treatment, yet resistance remains a significant clinical challenge. Sarcoma antigen 1 (SAGE1), a cancer-testis antigen, has been implicated in various malignancies, but its specific role in TNBC drug response and underlying mechanisms remain largely elusive. Using tumor specimens from two prospective TNBC trials, we found that high SAGE1 expression significantly correlates with inferior invasive disease-free survival in patients receiving carboplatin-containing chemotherapy. SAGE1 reduces carboplatin sensitivity in vitro and in vivo by accelerating DNA damage repair. Mechanistically, SAGE1 enhances global chromatin accessibility and H3K27ac enrichment at Fanconi Anemia (FA) pathway gene loci, interacting with p300 and BRD4 to promote H3K27ac deposition. The BET bromodomain inhibitor JQ1 reversed FA protein upregulation and restored carboplatin sensitivity in SAGE1-enriched cells. Furthermore, SAGE1 interacts with PARP1, and this interaction is associated with the regulation of PARP1 activity and with limited PARP inhibitor sensitivity. Notably, the triple combination of JQ1, carboplatin, and olaparib enhanced DNA damage and suppressed tumor growth in preclinical models. Thus, SAGE1 may contribute to an epigenetic-repair axis by facilitating chromatin opening and bolstering the FA pathway, and targeting this axis via combined carboplatin, PARP, and BET inhibition represents a promising therapeutic strategy for SAGE1-enriched TNBC.

papers.abstract: Pumitamig, an investigational bispecific antibody targeting programmed death ligand-1 and vascular endothelial growth factor A, has shown preliminary efficacy across several tumour types. We aimed to evaluate the safety and activity of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel as first-line treatment in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. In this single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial conducted at ten sites (hospitals and cancer centres) in China, patients aged 18-75 years with histologically documented, unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and one or more measurable lesion (as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours, version 1.1) received first-line pumitamig (20 mg/kg intravenously once every 2 weeks) plus nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. In phase 1b, six patients received pumitamig (20 mg/kg once every 2 weeks intravenously plus nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) and were monitored for treatment-emergent adverse events, before subsequent enrolment in phase 2. The primary endpoints were confirmed objective response rate and safety, assessed in the efficacy-evaluable population, defined as all patients who received one or more doses of study drug and had measurable disease at baseline and at least one efficacy assessment. This trial is registered with chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2200060400) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05918133), and is closed to recruitment. Between June 27, 2022, and March 15, 2023, 42 patients were enrolled, received one or more doses of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel (median duration of exposure 9·0 months, 95% CI 6·9-11·7) and had one or more tumour assessments. All patients were Chinese and female; median age was 53 years (IQR 41-60). At a median follow-up of 35·2 months (95% CI 33·0-36·1), the confirmed objective response rate was 73·8% (95% CI 58·0-86·1; 31 of 42 patients), including one complete response and 30 partial responses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were decreased neutrophil count (13 [31%] of 42 patients), decreased white blood cell count (11 [26%]), proteinuria (six [14%]), and febrile neutropenia (five [12%]). Nine (21%) patients reported 14 treatment-related serious adverse events (alanine aminotransferase increased n=2; febrile neutropenia n=2; pancreatitis n=2; and ascites, aspartate aminotransferase increased, abdominal distension, γ-glutamyltransferase increased, blood alkaline phosphatase increased, cataract, macular oedema, and retinal vein occlusion all n=1). Treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation of both nab-paclitaxel and pumitamig in four (10%) patients, discontinuation of nab-paclitaxel only in three (7%) patients, and discontinuation of pumitamig only in two (5%) patients. There were no treatment-related deaths. Treatment with first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel showed encouraging antitumour activity in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and a safety profile consistent with the mode of actions of both agents. These findings warrant further clinical evaluation in global phase 2 and 3 trials. Biotheus (BioNTech group). For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

papers.abstract: Digital health may extend cardiovascular care in communities with limited specialist access, but its effectiveness depends on whether communities have the infrastructure, devices, affordability, and capacity needed to use digital services. We linked national data on cardiometabolic disease burden, cardiology workforce, and digital readiness across 82,999 US census tracts. Among high-burden tracts in counties with no cardiologist or declining per-capita cardiologist supply, 4,765 (18.0%) tracts representing 19.9 million residents had higher digital readiness and were thus classified as deployment-priority tracts, whereas 21,752 (82.0%) tracts representing 74.1 million residents had lower readiness and were investment-priority tracts. Investment-priority tracts were spread across the urban-rural continuum and faced different barriers (adoption versus infrastructure). Contrasting classifications frequently occurred among neighboring census tracts within the same metropolitan area, highlighting geographic variation not captured by county-level targeting. Findings were broadly consistent across nine additional analyses with varying measures of readiness, workforce access, and classification thresholds. These findings provide a national framework for distinguishing communities where digital cardiovascular care may be deployed from those where infrastructure and adoption support may first be needed to enable equitable implementation.

papers.abstract: T cells engineered to express recombinant T cell receptors (TCRs) or chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) can induce durable clinical responses in solid and hematological malignancies. However, manufacturing is resource intensive and often yields highly differentiated, exhausted T cell products. To address this, we developed an antigen-scaffold (Ag-scaffold) technology that presents cognate antigen alongside stimulatory cytokines to preferentially expand genetically engineered T cells. We expanded CRISPR-Cas9- and lentivirally engineered TCR T cells with peptide MHC (pMHC)-presenting Ag-scaffolds and anti-CD19 CAR T cells with CD19-presenting Ag-scaffolds. By applying cognate pMHC Ag-scaffolds, we achieved on average 69% (±22%) antigen-specific T cells after 14 days of culture with a cytotoxic, proliferative profile. Ag-scaffold expansion enhanced initial TCR and CAR cytotoxicity; repeated rechallenges showed sustained control. In vivo, Ag-scaffold-expanded CRISPR-Cas9-engineered NY-ESO-1-specific TCR T cells and anti-CD19 CAR T cells also showed improved tumor control in lymphoma and solid tumor xenograft models compared to cells expanded with IL2/7/15.

papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) has emerged as a novel risk factor for pancreatic cancer, particularly early liver metastasis. However, the underlying mechanisms and effective therapeutic strategies remain largely unclear. Here, based on clinical databases, patient tissue samples, and single-cell sequencing of mouse models, we identified CD44 as a key contributor to MAFLD-associated pancreatic cancer progression. High CD44 expression was significantly associated with poor survival in patients with pancreatic cancer and was further elevated in MAFLD-associated liver metastatic lesions. Considering that the limited effects of single treatment, we developed a cationic DOTAP/cholesterol liposomal nanoplatform co-loaded with gemcitabine, IR780, and CD44 siRNA (GIR@Lip) for combined chemotherapy, photothermal therapy, and immunotherapy. GIR@Lip nanoparticles exhibited excellent size uniformity, stability, and photothermal conversion efficiency, which could efficiently inhibit KPC cells' viability, migration and invasion, downregulate CD44 expression and stimulate immune response. Furthermore, GIR@Lip efficiently accumulated in tumor tissues in vivo, exhibiting a significant reduction in liver metastatic lesions and remodeling the M1 type tumor associated macrophages (TAMs), CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Collectively, these findings identify CD44 as a potential therapeutic target for MAFLD-associated pancreatic cancer liver metastasis and highlight GIR@Lip as a promising multimodal strategy for its treatment.

papers.abstract: Nutrition is a key component of care for critically ill and surgical patients, but the organization of nutritional care and the involvement of dietitians in ICU and perioperative pathways remain variable. This survey aimed to describe respondent-reported nutritional care organization and dietitian involvement among healthcare professionals working in ICU and perioperative settings in France, with a focus on dietitian availability, clinical involvement, nutritional governance, and selected aspects of perioperative care. We conducted a voluntary cross-sectional survey among physicians and dietitians working in French ICU and perioperative settings. The survey was disseminated during the French Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care Medicine congress, through national professional nutrition and dietetics networks, and via social media. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Overall, 147 professionals responded, mainly ICU physicians and dietitians, and most worked in university hospitals. Among respondents, dietitian availability was reported in 67% of responses, but dedicated time was frequently limited. Involvement was mainly request-based, and participation in medical meetings or ward rounds was uncommon. A medical nutrition lead was identified in 44% of responses, a written nutrition protocol in 50%, and a task-sharing protocol allowing dietitian prescription in 9%. Reported practices suggest that dietitians are available in many French ICUs and contribute to perioperative care pathways. However, access to dietetic expertise does not necessarily translate into dedicated staffing, routine multidisciplinary participation, or structured nutritional governance. Strengthening local organization through medical leadership, written protocols, and multidisciplinary collaboration may help improve the implementation of nutritional care.

papers.abstract: Pulse contour devices estimate cardiac output (CO) from an invasive arterial blood pressure waveform. However, arterial catheters are generally used only in higher-risk patients. By contrast, automatic arm cuff devices are used for noninvasive BP monitoring in almost all hospital patients. Furthermore, these devices measure cuff pressure oscillations, which are directly related to pulsatile blood volume rather than BP. We hypothesised that automatic arm cuff devices can offer an effective means to monitor CO. A custom-built cuff device was used to measure cuff pressure and make a unique measurement of the volume of air pumped into and out of the cuff during linear deflation. Cuff device measurements, an invasive BP waveform from a radial artery catheter, and reference CO from pulmonary artery catheter bolus thermodilution were obtained during interventions from 24 liver transplant and 10 cardiac surgery patients (191 measurement sets). A basic analysis was applied to estimate CO in L min-1 as the product of heart rate, the maximum cuff pressure oscillation amplitude, the cuff-arm system compliance (derived from the cuff pressure-volume relationship), and the body-to-arm surface area ratio (derived from anthropometric information). The arm cuff-based method yielded a correlation of 0.61 (95% confidence interval 0.37-0.79) and a concordance rate of 83% (75%-91%) against the reference CO. For comparison, classic pulse contour analysis of the invasive BP waveform produced a correlation of 0.59 (0.37-0.75) and a concordance rate of 81% (72%-90%). These initial findings suggest potential for convenient CO monitoring using an automatic arm cuff device in surgical patients.

papers.abstract: Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is essential for improving survival, but reliance on endoscopy limits feasibility for population-wide screening. We developed ESCCseeker, a minimally invasive risk stratification tool based on peripheral blood mononuclear cells' DNA methylation. In a two-stage multicenter study in China, genome-wide profiling identifies distinct methylation markers between ESCC patients and controls. In the development and verification cohort, machine learning yields a model integrating eight differentially methylated positions with age, gender, SCC-Ag, and CYFRA21-1. ESCCseeker demonstrates robust performance (AUC: 0.987 training, 0.966 test, 0.943 verification), outperforming conventional biomarkers. In a prospective multicenter cohort, the predefined cutoff stratifies individuals into low- and high-risk groups. Restricting endoscopy to high-risk individuals reduces the number of endoscopies needed from 25.02 to 4.78, avoiding 83% of unnecessary procedures while preserving >90% detection sensitivity. These findings establish ESCCseeker as a reliable pre-endoscopic triage tool that minimizes unnecessary invasive procedures and prioritizes high-risk individuals. This trial was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500095967).

papers.abstract: The first-in-class allosteric BCR::ABL1 inhibitor asciminib has expanded the therapeutic landscape of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying secondary resistance remain incompletely understood. We investigated clinically observed asciminib resistance mutations by integrating structural modeling, hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), quantitative biochemical assays and molecular dynamics simulations. Resistance mutations were grouped into two mechanistically distinct classes: Mutations within the BCR::ABL1 myristate pocket (class I) and mutations located up to 40 Å from the asciminib binding site in the kinase N-lobe, SH2-kinase domain (KD) linker and SH3 domain (class II). HDX-MS demonstrated that asciminib induces conformational stabilization across the KD extending beyond the myristate pocket, establishing a long-range allosteric network. We show that class I mutations reduced asciminib affinity up to 90-fold, consistent with steric interference at the binding site. In contrast, class II mutations retained wildtype binding affinity despite conferring clinical resistance. Instead, the class II mutations F359I and M244V increased intrinsic kinase activity and enhanced BCR::ABL1 autophosphorylation, indicating overactivation. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed allosteric communication linking the myristate and ATP-binding pockets, which is disrupted by class II mutations. Together, these findings establish that asciminib resistance arises through two distinct mechanisms: direct impairment of drug binding or disruption of the asciminib binding-induced autoinhibited conformation. Our study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding resistance to allosteric BCR::ABL1 inhibitors and has important implications for resistance monitoring, combination therapies and therapeutic sequencing.

papers.abstract: The treatment landscape of ERBB2 (formerly HER2)-positive metastatic breast cancer has evolved substantially during the past decade, with emerging therapies challenging the long-standing induction-maintenance paradigm established by the CLEOPATRA trial (NCT00567190). However, optimal treatment selection, sequencing, and duration remain uncertain, particularly in the context of increasing therapeutic complexity and biologic heterogeneity. Taxane-based chemotherapy combined with trastuzumab and pertuzumab has long been the standard first-line induction regimen, followed by maintenance anti-ERBB2 therapy with or without endocrine therapy based on hormone receptor status. Recent data from the DESTINY-Breast09 trial (DB09; NCT04784715) demonstrate superior progression-free survival with trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab, supporting its recent US Food and Drug Administration approval and prompting questions regarding the necessity of chemotherapy, optimal duration of antibody-drug conjugate therapy, and the role of a dual ERBB2 blockade. Maintenance strategies have also expanded, particularly in hormone receptor-positive disease, with incorporation of endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors, as demonstrated in the PATINA trial (NCT02947685). The HER2CLIMB-05 trial (NCT05132582) provided an additional maintenance approach using a triplet anti-ERBB2 strategy. These nonchemotherapy maintenance options are designed to have fewer toxic effects and better quality of life than chemotherapy-based strategies. These developments raise questions regarding the necessity of chemotherapy, optimal duration of antibody-drug conjugate therapy, and the role of dual ERBB2 blockade. Emerging biomarker-driven approaches, including the HER2DX assay and circulating tumor DNA, remain investigational and are not yet part of routine clinical practice but aim to optimize treatment selection. Novel strategies, such as chemotherapy-free regimens and sequential multiagent approaches, as in the SAPPHO study (NCT06439693), are challenging traditional paradigms. The management of ERBB2-positive metastatic breast cancer is transitioning toward a more individualized approach that balances efficacy, toxic effects, and patient preferences. Integrating biomarker-driven strategies will be essential to optimize treatment selection, duration, and sequencing, with the goal of improving long-term outcomes while preserving quality of life.

papers.abstract: Professional oncology societies have invested in initiatives to enhance the racial and ethnic representation of the oncology physician workforce, particularly since 2020. Whether these initiatives have contributed to changes in the racial or ethnic representation among oncology trainees and nononcology trainees who provide cancer-related care is unclear. To assess trends in the distribution of underrepresented in medicine (URiM) physician trainees over time across oncology and nononcology specialties, with a focus on trends pre- and post-2020. The URiM category included individuals who identified as American Indian or Alaskan Native; Black or African American; Hispanic, Latino, or of Spanish origin; or Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander race or ethnicity. This repeated cross-sectional study used race and ethnicity data from the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education for trainees in medical, radiation, or surgical oncology; general surgery; and primary care from 2011 to 2025. Data were analyzed from April 2025 to August 2026. The proportion of URiM trainees was calculated by year and specialty. Segmented logistic regression was used to estimate the odds of being URiM overall and by specialty. Overall changes in the likelihood of a trainee being URiM post-2020 (level change) and the annual trend post-2020 (slope change) were estimated. There were 658 891 trainee observations in the cohort, of whom 113 937 trainees (17.3%) were URiM. The percentage of trainees who were URiM was relatively stable from 2011 (5435 trainees [16.1%]) to 2020 (8192 trainees [16.4%]), then increased to 13 345 trainees (20.4%) in 2025. After 2020, there was an overall 5% increase in the likelihood of a trainee being URiM (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03-1.08), as well as a 5% annual increase (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.05-1.06). Within individual specialties, significant post-2020 increases were observed in surgical oncology and general surgery. The post-2020 increase was greatest in radiation oncology (OR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.11-1.30). There was no statistically significant change in URiM representation among medical oncology trainees over the study period. This cross-sectional study found that the proportion of trainees who provide cancer care identifying as URiM increased from 2011 to 2025, particularly since 2020; however, URiM representation still did not match the diversity of the general US population in 2025.

papers.abstract: Biliary tract cancer (BTC) comprises a family of rare malignancies subclassified by anatomy and pathology. However, this classification scheme may obscure shared biology and limit patient stratification. Here, we tested whether BTC heterogeneity can be explained by coherent latent axes and evaluated the potential to unify diverse clinical and genomic factors under a tractable biological framework. Whole-genome and transcriptome sequencing was performed on 180 tumors enriched for tumor cells by laser capture microdissection to identify shared programs in BTC. Network integration across transcriptomic classes identified two consensus cancer subtypes (CCS). The CCS segregated with anatomical location of primary tumor, and gene expression marker analyses suggested that subtypes reflect tumor cell of origin differences. The CCS displayed strikingly divergent molecular landscapes, explaining more variance than anatomical location of the primary tumor. CCS-B tumors were mutationally loaded with clock-like and APOBEC signatures and extrachromosomal DNA, whereas CCS-A tumors were characterized by chromosome-arm deletions. This approach showed that harnessing the genomic and transcriptomic diversity of BTC provides insights into shared biology and improves stratification.

papers.abstract: Resistance to targeted therapies is frequently associated with stem-like features and partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Understanding whether these programs directly drive resistance or instead reflect increased phenotypic plasticity is needed to guide strategies for overcoming resistance. Here, we found that resistance to ALK inhibitors (ALKi) in non-small cell lung cancer was associated with increased phenotypic plasticity, reflected in enhanced adaptability to orthogonal stressors and increased metastatic potential, without intrinsic cross-resistance in short-term assays. Computational modeling and experimental validation studies showed that plasticity was progressively enriched over multi-step resistance trajectories. Lineage tracing and clonal analyses revealed a substantial, heritable intra-cell line variability in adaptation potential. High adaptation potential was associated with increased chromatin accessibility at EMT/stemness regulators. Adaptation potential could be enhanced by inducing stemness/EMT programs and suppressed by SOX2 knockdown or epigenetic inhibition, with corresponding effects on resistance. Collectively, these findings indicate that targeted therapy indirectly selects for cells with increased phenotypic plasticity, providing a common basis for the resistance-EMT association and the substrate for multifactorial resistance and metastatic competence. Constraining plasticity could delay resistance and extend response durability.

papers.abstract: To identify perioperative factors associated with the ionized-to-total magnesium (iMg/tMg) ratio at intensive care unit (ICU) admission and on postoperative day (POD) 1 after major open hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery. This single-center prospective observational study enrolled adults undergoing elective surgery. Paired iMg and tMg measurements were obtained at ICU admission and on POD 1. The primary analyses evaluated perioperative factors associated with the iMg/tMg ratio at each time point using univariable linear regression and multivariable linear regression with backward elimination. Exploratory analyses assessed temporal changes using paired t tests. Of 150 enrolled patients, 141 were analyzed. At ICU admission, the ratio was positively associated with iMg immediately after anesthesia induction (P = 0.007) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (P = 0.041), and negatively associated with anesthesia time (P = 0.005) and total cholesterol (P = 0.018). On POD 1, the ratio was positively associated with intraoperative non-Mg-containing fluid volume (P = 0.016), and negatively associated with operation time (P < 0.001), hypertension (P = 0.013), and albumin (P = 0.007). Model R2 values were 0.10 and 0.20 at ICU admission and on POD 1, respectively. In exploratory analyses, the mean ratio increased between postoperative measurements (0.659 to 0.713; P < 0.001). Mean iMg decreased from 0.589 mmol/L after induction to 0.545 at ICU admission, then increased to 0.640 on POD 1 (all P < 0.001). Perioperative factors associated with the iMg/tMg ratio differed between ICU admission and POD 1 after major open hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery. Both models had limited explanatory power. These findings should be interpreted in relation to sampling time and require independent validation before informing clinical management.

papers.abstract: Bispecific antibodies targeting vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/PD-1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) pathways represent a promising therapeutic strategy for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). HB0025 is a novel bispecific antibody fusion targeting PD-L1 and VEGF. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of HB0025 plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced, driver variant-negative NSCLC. This open-label, multicenter, phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial enrolled patients with stage IIIB/C or IV NSCLC without sensitizing EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 alterations across 13 hospitals in China. Participants included those with nonsquamous NSCLC and squamous NSCLC. Patients were enrolled from January 15, 2024, to May 21, 2025. Data cutoff was April 20, 2026. Patients received intravenous 10-mg/kg HB0025 every 3 weeks or 20-mg/kg HB0025 every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy: pemetrexed/carboplatin for nonsquamous and paclitaxel/carboplatin for squamous for up to 6 cycles, followed by HB0025 maintenance (with pemetrexed for nonsquamous) until disease progression or unacceptable toxic effects. The primary end points were safety and investigator-assessed objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors, version 1.1. The secondary end points included disease control rate, duration of response, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Treatment efficacy was evaluable in 169 enrolled patients. The nonsquamous cohort included 85 patients (median [IQR] age, 63.0 [58.0-68.0] years; 26 [30.6%] female and 59 [69.4%] male patients), and the squamous cohort included 84 patients (median [IQR] age, 65.0 [60.0-69.0] years; 6 [7.1%] female and 78 [92.9%] male patients). In the nonsquamous cohort, confirmed ORR was 36.4% (95% CI, 17.2%-59.3%) and 57.1% (95% CI, 44.1%-69.5%) in the 10-mg/kg and 20-mg/kg dose groups, respectively. In the squamous cohort, ORR reached 68.2% (95% CI, 45.1%-86.1%) and 74.2% (95%, 61.5%-84.5%) at the respective doses. Median PFS was 12.52 months (95% CI, 10.15-16.56) in the nonsquamous cohort and 14.78 months (95% CI, 11.30 to not estimable) in the squamous cohort. The 12-month PFS rates were 54.3% (95% CI, 41.6%-65.3%) and 62.1% (95% CI, 49.9%-72.1%) in the nonsquamous and squamous cohorts, and the 12-month OS rates were 75.8% (95% CI, 65.0%-83.7%) and 85.5% (95% CI, 75.8%-91.5%) , respectively. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 56 of 85 patients (65.9%) in the nonsquamous cohort and 51 of 84 (60.7%) in the squamous cohort, mainly as hematologic toxic effects. Any-grade immune-related adverse events related to HB0025 occurred in 20 patients (23.5%) in the nonsquamous cohort and 21 patients (25%) in the squamous cohort. In this phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, HB0025 plus chemotherapy showed promising antitumor activity and manageable safety in patients with advanced, driver variant-negative NSCLC in both nonsquamous and squamous histologic types, supporting further evaluation in randomized phase 3 clinical trials.
